dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَبارَكَ): al-baraka is the increase of good and its abundance. The increase may be sensory or abstract, i.e. His good has increased and multiplied, or He has risen above everything and is exalted above it in His attributes and acts. Further, (تبارك) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb that does not conjugate: no imperfect, imperative or active participle comes from it, it has no maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is not used of other than Allah the Exalted. A discussion of the jāmid [verb] will come in the section on benefits.
(الْفُرْقانَ): the Qur'an, because it distinguishes (faraqa) between truth and falsehood; it is also said: because it was revealed in separate parts (mufarraqan) at many times. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "faraqtu bayna al-shayʾayn farqan, of the pattern of qatala: I separated its parts; and faraqtu bayna al-ḥaqq wal-bāṭil: I also separated. This is the high usage, and in it the Seven [readers] read His saying, Exalted is He: «فَافْرُقْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ». In one dialect it is of the pattern of ḍaraba, and some of the Successors read it so. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: 'faraqtu bayna al-kalāmayn fa-ftaraqā', with the light form, and 'farraqtu bayna al-ʿabdayn fa-tafarraqā', with the doubled form; so he made the light form for abstract meanings and the doubled form for concrete things. What others relate is that they have the same meaning, and the doubling is for intensification." This root has many branches in the language, and we shall set out for you some of them that will delight the mind. Al-furqān is the maṣdar of "faraqa bayna al-shayʾayn" when he separates between two things. The Qur'an was named by it because it separates between truth and falsehood, or because it was not revealed all at once but separated, its parts set apart from one another in revelation. Do you not see His saying: «وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا»? The more apparent is the second meaning, because in the sūra, a few verses later, there is: «وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك» [Translator's note: the source prints «نزلوا»; the verse reads «نزل»].
Allah the Exalted said «كذلك», i.e. We revealed it in separate parts thus, so that We may strengthen your heart with it. So describing it as al-Furqān at the beginning of the sūra is like an introduction and preparation for what comes afterwards. The Encyclopaedia of Islam considered the word furqān to be of unknown origin, and this is a clear error and an evident delusion, as you have seen from the derivation of the word. It is said: "faraqa lī al-ṭarīqu furūqan" and "infaraqa infirāqan", when two roads face you and it becomes clear which of them must be taken; "a road afraq": clear; "he gathered the tafārīq of his goods", i.e. what was scattered of them; "Allah struck with the truth on the tongue of al-Fārūq"; "al-furqān shone forth", i.e. the dawn; "this is clearer than the cleaving of dawn (falaq al-ṣubḥ) and the parting of dawn (faraq al-ṣubḥ)"; you say "an afraq path", as if it were the parting [of hair]; "he is swifter than the farīq of the horses", which is the one that outstrips them — faʿīl in the sense of mufāʿil, because when it outstrips them it parts from them; "furūq of grey hair appeared on the back of his head", i.e. white streaks of it; "he has nothing but a firq and a farīqa of sheep", i.e. a few; a Bedouin saw some boys and said: "These are a bad firq (band)"; "you are nothing but a farūqa (very fearful)"; "farqun khayrun min ḥubb", i.e. that you be feared is better than that you be loved; "the feverish one and the madman recovered (afraqa)", and "he is in afrāq (recovery) from his fever". Among the figurative usages: "I acquainted him with the mafāriq of the matter", i.e. its clear aspects. In al-Lisān and al-Asās: "Greyness appeared in his mafriq and his farq (parting of the hair); I saw the gleam of perfume in their mafāriq; the comber parted her head such-and-such a parting; a parted head (raʾs mafrūq); an afraq cock: whose comb is split; an afraq camel: one with two humps; a man afraq of teeth: one with gaps between them; a fāriq she-camel: one in labour [Translator's note: the source prints «ما خض», evidently for «ماخض»] which has left the camels, fleeing from the pain of labour; she-camels furuq, fawāriq and mafārīq; she has become fāriq (faraqat furūqan); and the cloud is likened to her. Dhū al-Rumma said:
أو مزنة فارق يجلو غواربها ... تبوّج البرق والظلماء علجوم
(Or a rain-cloud like a camel in labour, its crests lit up by the flashing of lightning, while the darkness is dense.)"

* I'rab:
(تَبارَكَ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقانَ عَلى عَبْدِهِ لِيَكُونَ لِلْعالَمِينَ نَذِيراً) (تبارك) is an inflexible past verb, as preceded in the section on vocabulary; (الذي) is its fāʿil (agent); the clause (نزل الفرقان) is the ṣila (relative clause); (على عبده) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزل). The lām is of cause (taʿlīl); (يكون) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of cause; the noun of (يكون) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; and (نذيرا) is the khabar (predicate) of (يكون). (الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَداً) This relative noun may be a badal (substitute) of the first relative noun, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), so that its position is nominative; and it may be accusative by way of praise; or what follows it completes the ṣila of the first relative noun. (له) is a fronted khabar and (ملك السموات والأرض) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (لم يتخذ ولدا) is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيراً) Conjoined to what preceded. (له) is the fronted khabar of (يكن) and (شريك) its postponed noun; (في الملك) is attached to (شريك). (خلق) is also conjoined to what preceded, so it is part of the completion of the reason for what is before it [Translator's note: so in the source, «من تمام العلة»; perhaps «من تمام الصلة», "part of the completion of the ṣila"]. (كل شيء) is the object of (خلق). (فقدره): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قدره) is a past verb with a latent agent and a direct object; and (تقديرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً لا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ) (واتخذوا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, set out to establish the state and worship of the disbelievers. (من دونه) is in the position of the second object of (اتخذوا) and (آلهة) is the first object of (اتخذوا). The clause (لا يخلقون شيئا) is an adjective of (آلهة) — one of seven adjectives that will come listed in succession. (وهم يخلقون): the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (يخلقون), in the passive form, is the khabar; this is the second adjective. The meaning of their being created is that their worshippers carve them and shape them. (وَلا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ ضَرًّا وَلا نَفْعاً وَلا يَمْلِكُونَ مَوْتاً وَلا حَياةً وَلا نُشُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا يملكون) is a clause conjoined to what preceded, and (ضرا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); this is the third adjective. (ولا نفعا) is the fourth adjective; (ولا يملكون موتا) is the fifth; (ولا حياة) is the sixth; and (ولا نشورا) is the seventh. Al-nushūr is the raising of the dead. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هَذا إِلَّا إِفْكٌ افْتَراهُ) A resumptive statement set out to begin relating their falsehoods, refuting and rebutting them. (الذين) is the fāʿil of (قال), and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (إن) is negative; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إفك) is the khabar of (هذا); and the clause (افتراه) is an adjective of (إفك). (وَأَعانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ فَقَدْ جاؤُ ظُلْماً وَزُوراً) (وأعانه) is conjoined to (افتراه); (عليه) is attached to (أعانه), the pronoun referring to the fabricated lie; (قوم) is the fāʿil and (آخرون) an adjective of (قوم). By them they mean the People of the Book who supplied him, as they claimed, with reports of past nations and extinct generations. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (قد) is a particle of verification; (جاءوا) is a verb and its agent; it has taken on the meaning of «فعل» (did), so it was made transitive as that is, and (ظلما) is its object. It may also be in its original sense, so (ظلما) is parsed as accusative by removal of the preposition, or accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted [as a participle], i.e. "being unjust"; and (زورا) is conjoined to (ظلما). (وَقالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ اكْتَتَبَها فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قالوا) is a verb and its agent; (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause (اكتتبها) is a ḥāl. (أساطير الأولين) may also be parsed as a mubtadaʾ with the clause (اكتتبها) as khabar. (فهي): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (تملى) the khabar; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; (عليه) is attached to (تملى); (بكرة) is an adverb attached to (تملى) and (أصيلا) is conjoined to (بكرة). The meaning of «تملى عليه» is "it is read to him so that he may have it copied by means of someone who writes for him", because he (peace be upon him) was unlettered.
(قُلْ أَنْزَلَهُ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; the clause (أنزله) is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (الذي) is the direct object [Translator's note: so in the source; (الذي) is the fāʿil of (أنزله)]; the clause (يعلم السر) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (في السموات والأرض) is a ḥāl; and the clause (إنه كان…) (the verse) gives the reason for what preceded, so it has no grammatical position. Its parsing has preceded often.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «فَقَدْ جاؤُ ظُلْماً وَزُوراً» there is ordered laff wa-nashr (involution and evolution). It has preceded in this book that laff wa-nashr is a device comprising the mention of several things, in detail or in summary, followed by the mention of what belongs to each of them without specifying, trusting that the listener will distinguish what belongs to each and refer it to what it belongs to. We have illustrated each of its two kinds sufficiently. As for this verse, His saying, Exalted is He, «فَقَدْ جاؤُ ظُلْماً وَزُوراً» contains [injustice in] making the inimitable speech a fabricated lie picked up from the Jews or others of the People of the Book; and falsehood (zūr) in attributing to it what it is free of.

* Benefits:
The inflexible (jāmid) verb:
The jāmid verb is one that resembles the particle in that it conveys a meaning stripped of the time and the event that are considered in verbs; so, like it, it keeps to one form in expression: it does not accept change from form to form but keeps to one form that it never leaves. Such are: (عسى), (ليس), and (هب) in the sense of "suppose, assume" — of its root with this meaning only the imperative occurs, so it is an inflexible imperative verb. As for (هب) derived from al-hiba (giving), its past is (وهب) and its imperfect (يهب); likewise (هب) derived from al-hayba (awe) is a conjugating imperative verb, whose past is (هاب) and imperfect (يهاب). [Also] (نعم) and (بئس). It either keeps to the past form, like (عسى), (ليس), (نعم), (بئس) and «تبارك الله»; or to the imperfect form, like (يهيط), whose meaning is "he shouts and hisses" — it is said: "he has kept on yahīṭu hayṭan since today" — and it is an imperfect with no past, as in Lisān al-ʿArab and Tāj al-ʿArūs. It is said: "he is still in hayṭ and mayṭ", with fatḥa on the first letter of both, and "in hiyāṭ and miyāṭ", with kasra on the first letter of both, i.e. clamour, mischief and uproar. It is also said of "hiyāṭ and miyāṭ":
in approaching and moving away; al-hiyāṭ is coming forward and al-miyāṭ is going back; al-hāʾiṭ is the one coming and al-māʾiṭ the one going; al-muhāyaṭa and al-hiyāṭ are shouting and uproar; and it is said "between them is muhāyaṭa, mumāyaṭa, musāyaṭa and mushāyaṭa", i.e. discordant talk. [Or it keeps to the imperative form,] like (هب), (هات), (تعال), and (هلم) in the dialect of Tamīm, because for them it is a verb that accepts its sign, so the pronouns are attached to it; but in the dialect of Ḥijāz it is a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr), because for them it is in one form for all. Its discussion will come in its place. Among the jāmid verbs is (قلّ), in the past form, for pure negation. When the redundant (zāʾida) (ما) is attached to it, it restrains it from governing, so that then only a verb follows it, and it has no fāʿil (agent), since it runs the course of a negative particle, as in: «قلما فعلت هذا» and «قلما أفعله», i.e. "I did not do" and "I do not do". Of this is the poet's saying:
قلما يبرح اللبيب إلى ما ... يورث المجد داعيا أو مجيبا
(Seldom does the intelligent man cease to call to, or answer, what bequeaths glory.)
i.e. the intelligent man never ceases calling. A noun may follow it under poetic necessity, as in his saying:
صددت فأطولت الصدود وقلما ... وصال على طول الصدود يدوم
(You turned away and prolonged the aversion, and seldom does union endure through long aversion.)
By your saying «قلما أفعل» the affirmation of doing [it] rarely may be intended, as in al-Kulliyyāt of Abū al-Baqāʾ, though its frequent use is for pure negation. Like (قلما) in not conjugating are (طالما), (كثرما), (قصرما) and (شدما): the (ما) in them is redundant, for emphasis, restraining them from governing, so they have no fāʿil and only a verb follows them; they are like (قلما). Among the jāmid verbs is their saying «سقط في يده», meaning he regretted, was perplexed, slipped and erred; it keeps to the form of the passive past. Allah the Exalted said: «وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ». Its discussion has preceded.

dervis-irab:7-12.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا: مالِ هذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْواقِ) A resumptive statement set out to begin explaining their vile [claims] which they spread as rumours about the Messenger; they are six, as will come. (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ما) is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (لهذا) its khabar (predicate); (الرسول) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; the clause (يأكل الطعام) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and this is the first fabrication. (يأكل الطعام) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يمشي في الأسواق) is conjoined to it, and this is the second fabrication. The meaning of eating food and walking in the markets will come in the section on rhetoric.
(لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيراً) (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (أنزل) is a passive past verb; (عليه) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «إليه»] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (ملك) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya); (يكون) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ of causation, because it is the answer to the urging. Its noun is latent, its implied form being "he", i.e. the angel; (معه) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (نذيرا) is the khabar of (يكون), i.e. so that the two of them support each other in warning and making afraid. This is the third fabrication. (أَوْ يُلْقى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْها) (أو) is a conjunction; (يلقى) is a passive imperfect verb; (كنز) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إليه) is attached to (يلقى). (أو تكون له جنة) is conjoined to what preceded, and the clause (يأكل منها) is an adjective of (جنة). These two verbs are conjoined to (أنزل), because it has the meaning of "is sent down" (yunzalu); it is not permissible to conjoin them to (فيكون), made accusative in the answer, because they are included within the urging, and so are conjoined to [what precedes] its answer. These two are the fourth and fifth fabrications. (وَقالَ الظَّالِمُونَ: إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الظالمون) is a verb and its agent; (إن) is negative; (تتبعون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (رجلا) is the direct object and (مسحورا) an adjective. This is the sixth and last fabrication.
(انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ فَضَلُّوا فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا) (انظر) is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; (لك) is attached to (ضربوا) and (الأمثال) is the direct object. (فضلوا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ضلوا) is a past verb and its agent. (فلا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (يستطيعون سبيلا) is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object. (تَبارَكَ الَّذِي إِنْ شاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْراً مِنْ ذلِكَ) A resumptive statement set out to establish His transcendence, Glorified is He, and His exaltation above what they say. (تبارك الذي) is a verb and its agent; al-Zamakhsharī, al-Jalāl and others assumed an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the good of the One who". (إن) is conditional; (شاء) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (جعل) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لك) is the second object of (جعل) and (خيرا) the first object of (جعل); (من ذلك) is attached to (خيرا); the demonstrative refers to what they proposed of the treasure and the garden. (جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُوراً) (جنات) is a badal of (خيرا); the clause (تجري) is an adjective of (جنات); (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) and (الأنهار) is the fāʿil of (تجري). (يجعل) is an imperfect verb conjoined to the position of (جعل), which falls as the apodosis of the condition — an important discussion of the protasis and its apodosis will come in the section on benefits. (لك) is the second object and (قصورا) the first object. (بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالسَّاعَةِ وَأَعْتَدْنا لِمَنْ كَذَّبَ بِالسَّاعَةِ سَعِيراً) (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb): He digressed from rebuking them by relating their earlier rumours to relating their denial of the Hour. (كذبوا) is a verb and its agent; (بالساعة) is attached to (كذبوا); (أعتدنا) is a verb and its agent; (لمن) is attached to (أعتدنا); the clause (كذب بالساعة) is the ṣila of (من); and (سعيرا) is the direct object. The meaning is:
We have prepared for these deniers a great fire. The relative noun was put in place of the pronoun, and «الساعة» in place of its pronoun, for intensity of rebuke; its parallels have passed in the sections on rhetoric. The tanwīn of (سعيرا) is for magnification, i.e. a great fire, as we mentioned. (إِذا رَأَتْهُمْ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً) This conditional clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective of (سعيرا), because it is feminine in the sense of «النار». (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause (رأتهم) is in the position of genitive by (إذا)'s being annexed to it; (من مكان) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause (سمعوا) is the apodosis; (لها) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective [of what follows it]; (تغيظا) is the direct object and (زفيرا) is conjoined to it. A lengthy section on this expression will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Two remarkable metonymies (kināya):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَقالُوا مالِ هذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْواقِ» there is a metonymy for answering the call of nature, since it necessarily accompanies eating food; its explanation has passed in detail in Sūrat al-Māʾida, so refresh your memory of it. In «يمشي في الأسواق» there is a metonymy for seeking a livelihood. After these two remarkable metonymies, look at the account of their confused notions and feverish fancies: how they first proposed that he be an angel, [descending] to the proposal that he be a man with an angel accompanying him, so that the two might support each other in warning and making afraid; then they descended further and said: even if he is not aided by an angel, let him be aided by a treasure cast to him from the sky, with which he might gain strength and not need to earn a livelihood; then they descended and were content that he be a man with a garden from which he eats and gains provision as the wealthy gain provision. See how it depicts the notions of the confused soul and the states of its wavering.
2- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun:
In His saying «وقال الظالمون» the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun; it has been alluded to before with its examples. By "the wrongdoers" He meant them themselves, for they are the ones who spoke first; the overt noun was put in place of the pronoun only to record against them the description of wrongdoing and transgressing the limit.
3- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): Affirming sight for Hell, and the audible fury and rising roar, is a matter that has occupied the scholars greatly. As for Ahl al-Sunna, they take all of that as literal and do not interpret it as figurative: for Hell's seeing is possible and the power of Allah the Exalted is capable [of it], and the apparent texts have concurred on the occurrence of this possible thing and that Allah the Exalted creates for it sensory and rational perception. Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He, «سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظاً», and its disputing with Paradise, and its saying «هل من مزيد», and its complaining to its Lord, whereupon He permitted it two breaths — and other apparent texts which there is no way to interpret otherwise, since there is no need for that? They said: "If the door of interpretation and figurative reading were opened in the states of the Return, whoever takes that road would be flung into the valley of misguidance." As for hearing fury, when fury is not heard, Ahl al-Sunna answered with three answers, which we list below:
a- It is by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the sound of its fury".
b- It is by omission of a verb, its implied form being "they heard and saw fury and roaring", so that each refers back to what befits it, i.e. they saw fury and heard roaring.
c- That (سمعوا) be made to include a meaning comprising both things, i.e. they perceived in it fury and roaring.
As for His saying (رأتهم), some said it is by way of inversion (qalb), i.e. they saw it; or it is by an omission, its implied form being "its keepers (zabāniya) saw them".
As for the Muʿtazila, they take all of that as figurative and make Hell's seeing of the kind of their saying "the houses of Banū so-and-so see one another and face one another"; it then enters the category of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), which has been discussed often before.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding His saying «إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد»: from a distance of a hundred years' journey. That is when Hell is brought, led by seventy thousand reins, each rein pulled by seventy thousand angels; were it left free, it would come upon every righteous and wicked person. «سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا»: it gives a roar such that no tear remains but falls; then it gives the second roar, and hearts are torn from their places, and the uvulas and throats are torn.
4- Ḥusn al-ittibāʿ (excellent following):
Further, the poets have gazed at the heaven of these eloquent expressions, in what falls under ḥusn al-ittibāʿ: that the speaker takes up a meaning invented by someone else and follows it so well that he deserves it and it is adjudged to him rather than to the first. This category is specific to the speech of created beings and what some of them took from others; nothing of the Mighty Qur'an has a place in it, for the Qur'an is followed, not a follower [Translator's note: the source prints «مبتع», evidently for «متَّبِع»]. However, when the poets gaze at its heaven and follow it well, it becomes as if it were included in the string of this device. Al-Farazdaq said:
يكاد يمسكه عرفان راحته ... ركن الحطيم إذا ما جاء يستلم
(The corner of al-Ḥaṭīm almost holds him fast, recognising his palm, when he comes to touch it.)
He attributed the acts of a rational being to what is not rational. Abū Tammām followed his pattern and said:
لو يعلم الركن من قد جاء يلثمه ... لخرّ يلثم منه موطىء القدم
(If the Corner knew who has come to kiss it, it would fall down to kiss the place where his foot treads.)
Al-Buḥturī followed in the footsteps of Abū Tammām and said:
فلو أن مشتاقا تكلف فوق ما ... في وسعه لسعى إليك المنبر
(If a yearning one could strain beyond what is in its power, the pulpit would have come striving to you.)
And al-Mutanabbī followed al-Buḥturī in that and said:
لو تعقل الشجر التي قابلتها ... مدّت محيية إليك الأغصنا
(If the trees you faced had understanding, they would stretch out their branches to you in greeting.)
This is a broad category; many examples of it will come.

* Benefits:
The protasis and the apodosis:
It is not a condition that the protasis and the apodosis be of one kind; rather, sometimes:
1- They are both imperfect, as in «وإن تعودوا نعد».
2- They are both past, as in «وإن عدتم عدنا».
3- They differ, past then imperfect, as in «من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه». This is good only because the reliance in meaning is on the khabar of kāna, which is imperfect, so it is as though He said: "whoever wants, We increase for him."
4- They are the reverse of it, imperfect then past; this is rare, and some restricted it to poetry. Of it there occurs in the ḥadīth his saying ﷺ: «من يقم ليلة القدر احتسابا غفر له» ("Whoever stands [in prayer] on the Night of Decree seeking reward, he is forgiven"), narrated by al-Bukhārī.
Further, when the protasis occurs as a past verb, both jussive and nominative are permissible in its apodosis, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
وإن أتاه خليل يوم مسغبة ... يقول لا غائب مالي ولا حرم
(If a friend comes to him on a day of famine, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)
with (يقول) in the nominative. Ibn Mālik said: «وبعد ماض رفعك الجزا حسن» ("After a past [protasis], your putting the apodosis in the nominative is good") [Translator's note: the source prints «رفعك الخبر أحسن»; the line of the Alfiyya reads «وبعد ماض رفعك الجزا حسن»]. What made that good is that, since the particle did not govern the wording of the protasis, because it is past, despite its nearness, it does not govern the apodosis given its remoteness. For that reason «ويجعل لك قصورا» was read with (يجعل) in the nominative, conjoined to (جعل). Some wanted to fault Shawqī for his saying:
إن رأتني تميل عني كأن لم ... يك بيني وبينها أشياء
(If she sees me, she turns away from me, as if there had been nothing between me and her.)
and the preceding rule escaped them.

dervis-irab:13-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُقَرَّنِينَ): from qarranahu, with a doubled rāʾ: he gathered him and bound him tightly; it is said "qarrantu al-asārā fī al-ḥibāl" (I bound the captives together in ropes). Its triliteral verb is qarana yaqrinu, of the pattern of ḍaraba yaḍribu: qarana al-shayʾa bil-shayʾ, he tied it to it and joined it to it; qarana al-thawrayn, he put the two oxen under one yoke; and qarana al-baʿīrayn, he joined the two camels in one rope. In His saying, Exalted is He, «مقرنين» it conveys two things: al-taṣfīd (fettering), i.e. binding the feet, and joining the hands and necks with chains.
(ثُبُوراً): destruction. It is said: thabarahu Allāh: He destroyed him with a lasting destruction after which he does not revive; hence the people of the Fire cry: "wā thubūrāh!" (O destruction!). "Mā thabaraka ʿan ḥājatik?": what held you back? And "this is the mashbar of so-and-so (a woman)" [Translator's note: so in the source; the lexicons have «مَثْبِر», mathbir]: the place where she gives birth, where the childbed bleeding afflicts her.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا أُلْقُوا مِنْها مَكاناً ضَيِّقاً مُقَرَّنِينَ دَعَوْا هُنالِكَ ثُبُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause (ألقوا) is genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and it [the adverb] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), which is (دعوا). (ألقوا) is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (منها) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (مكانا), because it was originally an adjective of it; (مكانا) is an adverb attached to (ألقوا); (ضيقا) is an adjective of (مكانا); and (مقرنين) is a ḥāl of the wāw in (ألقوا). The clause (دعوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) of (دعوا); (هنالك) is a demonstrative in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (دعوا): in that place. The meaning of (دعوا) is "they called out". (ثبورا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (دعوا), and it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of (دعوا). Al-Zajjāj said: (ثبورا) is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "we have been destroyed a destruction". It is also said it is accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu); and it is said it is vocative, i.e. they say: "O destruction, come! This is your time", for destruction is lighter for them than what they are in.
(لا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُوراً واحِداً وَادْعُوا ثُبُوراً كَثِيراً) The clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying, its implied form being "so it will be said to them", and this omitted [element] is conjoined to what precedes it.
(لا) is prohibitive; (تدعوا) is an imperfect verb made jussive by the prohibitive (لا); the wāw is the fāʿil of (تدعوا); (ثبورا) — it has preceded that it is a direct object or a mafʿūl muṭlaq; (ادعوا) is an imperative verb; the parsing of (ثبورا) has preceded; and (كثيرا) is an adjective of (ثبورا). It was expressed with multiplicity and oneness was denied of it because it is of many kinds, each of which is a destruction because of its severity and horror; or because, every time their skins are roasted through, they are given other skins in exchange, so there is no limit and no end to their destruction. (قُلْ: أَذلِكَ خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ كانَتْ لَهُمْ جَزاءً وَمَصِيراً) (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is necessarily latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you". The hamza is an interrogative for reproach and sarcasm — further discussion of the rhetoric of this verse will come. (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (خير) the khabar (predicate); (أم) is a conjunction and (جنة الخلد) is conjoined to (ذلك); the relative noun is an adjective of (جنة الخلد); the clause (وعد المتقون) is a verbal clause of a verb and its deputy agent, the ṣila (relative clause). The clause (كانت لهم) is a ḥāl of (جنة الخلد); (لهم) is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective; the noun of (كانت) is latent, its implied form being "it"; (جزاء) is the khabar of (كانت) and (مصيرا) is conjoined to (جزاء). (لَهُمْ فِيها ما يَشاؤُنَ خالِدِينَ كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ وَعْداً مَسْؤُلًا) The clause is a second ḥāl of (جنة الخلد). (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) is a ḥāl; (ما) is a postponed mubtadaʾ and the clause (يشاءون) is the ṣila; (خالدين) is a permanent ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima) of the hāʾ in (لهم) or of the wāw in (يشاءون). (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, referring to the promise understood from His saying (وعد المتقون), or to (ما يشاءون); (على ربك) is a ḥāl because it was an adjective of (وعدا); and (مسئولا) is an adjective of (وعدا).

* Benefits:
The meaning of preference (tafḍīl):
What is understood from the elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl) is a difference of degree between two shared qualities. So how did He say «أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد», when it is known that there is no good whatsoever in the Fire? The like of this question has preceded, and the answer is what Sībawayh related from the Arabs:
"Is misery dearer to you or happiness?", when it is known that happiness is dearer to him. It is also said [Translator's note: the source prints «وقبل», evidently for «وقيل»] that it is not of the category of the elative noun at all, but is rather like your saying "with him is good (khayr)".
Among what one cannot avoid drawing attention to is that the apparent sense of His saying, Exalted is He, «لَهُمْ فِيها ما يَشاؤُنَ», requires — by the generality of the relative noun — that if one of them wished for the rank of someone above him, such as the prophets, he would attain it, so that no difference would remain between the deficient and the perfect. It also requires that if one of them wished to intercede for someone among the people of the Fire, such as his son or his father, his intercession would be accepted; and that conflicts with the knowledge that the punishment of the disbeliever is everlasting. Al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī answered this misleading impression with his saying: "Perhaps He confines the aspirations of each group to what befits its rank, and He, Exalted is He, does not cast into their minds that they should attain more than they have attained, or seek increase over the waters of bliss rippling over them in which they swim." The ḥadīths are abundant concerning the degrees of Paradise and their differences. Al-Bukhārī narrated from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there are a hundred degrees that Allah has prepared for those who strive in the path of Allah; between every two degrees is as between the heaven and the earth."

dervis-irab:17-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُوراً): al-būr, with ḍamma on the bāʾ: the corrupt in which there is no good. It is said "a būr woman" and "a būr people"; the singular and the plural are described by it. Al-būr of land is what has not been cultivated. It may also be the plural of bāʾir, like ʿāʾidh and ʿūdh. In al-Asās, al-Lisān and al-Tāj: "So-and-so, to him his nūr, and upon you his būr", i.e. his destruction [Translator's note: so in the source]; "a būr people"; "they settled [their people] in the abode of perdition (dār al-bawār)"; and "Bawāri [perdition] descended on the disbelievers". Abū Mukʿit al-Asadī said:
قتلت فكان تظالما وتباغيا ... إن التظالم في الصديق بوار
لو كان أول ما أتيت تهارشت ... أولاد عرج عليك عند وجار
(You killed, and it was mutual wrong and aggression; wronging one another among friends is ruin. Had it been the first thing you did, the cubs of the lame [hyena] would have fought over you by a den.)
He made it [i.e. bawāri] a proper name for hyenas, so definiteness and femininity came together. Among the figurative usages: "the wares were stagnant (bārat)", i.e. found no market; "a stagnant (bāʾira) market"; and "the unmarried woman bārat" when no one desires her.

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ وَما يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) A resumptive statement set out to connect with what He mentioned at the beginning of the sūra, namely His saying «واتخذوا من دونه آلهة».
The adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied «اذكر» (remember), conjoined to (قل). The clause (يحشرهم), with yāʾ and with nūn [as variant readings], is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ما) is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ, or accusative as an object of accompaniment (maʿiyya). He gave the non-rational predominance (taghlīb) over the rational and so used «ما» rather than «من», because among those worshipped are rational beings. It is also said that the word «ما» is coined for all [kinds], or that He means the idols, because they will speak with the tongue of their state, as is said of the testimony of the hands and feet.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is it valid to use «ما» for rational beings?
I say: it is coined for generality, for rational beings and others, as evidenced by your saying, when you see a figure from afar: 'What (mā) is it?' Then, if you are told: 'A human being', you say at that point: 'Who (man) is he?'"
The clause (يعبدون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), and (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَيَقُولُ: أَأَنْتُمْ أَضْلَلْتُمْ عِبادِي هؤُلاءِ أَمْ هُمْ ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ)
(فيقول) is conjoined to (يحشرهم). (أأنتم): the hamza is for the interrogative of reproach; (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (أضللتم) the khabar (predicate); (عبادي) is the direct object; (هؤلاء) is a demonstrative, an adjective of (عبادي), i.e. those pointed to, or a badal (substitute) of (عبادي). (أم) is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (ضلوا) its khabar. (السبيل) is accusative by removal of the preposition, because «ضلّ» is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «أضلّه», and the analogy would be «ضلّ عن السبيل», except that they dropped the preposition, just as they dropped it in «هداه الطريق», whose origin is «إلى الطريق» and «للطريق». (قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ) (سبحانك) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "declaring You far above what does not befit You". (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective past verb; the clause (ينبغي) is the khabar of kāna; (لنا) is attached to (ينبغي); (أن) and what falls within its scope are the fāʿil (agent) of (ينبغي), so the noun of kāna is latent — or the fāʿil of (ينبغي) is latent [Translator's note: so in the source]. (من دونك) is the second object of (نتخذ); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (أولياء) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the first object of (نتخذ) — or the reverse. The correct view is that His saying (من أولياء) is the first object, because it is the one in which «من» may be redundant, unlike the second. You say: «ما اتخذت من أحد وليا» ("I did not take anyone as a protector"), and in the most eloquent usage it is not permissible [to say] «ما اتخذت أحدا من ولي».
(وَلكِنْ مَتَّعْتَهُمْ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى نَسُوا الذِّكْرَ وَكانُوا قَوْماً بُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) is lightened and inoperative (muhmala), for rectification (istidrāk); (متعتهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object. (وآباءهم): the wāw is a conjunction or of accompaniment, and (آباءهم) is conjoined to the hāʾ or is an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu). (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (نسوا الذكر) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (كانوا) is kāna and its noun; (قوما) is its khabar and (بورا) an adjective. (فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ بِما تَقُولُونَ فَما تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفاً وَلا نَصْراً) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), because it is consequent upon an omitted [element], and because it is a sudden confrontation with argument and binding proof, especially when iltifāt (shift of address) and the omission of the saying are joined to it. This expression is very eloquent, and it has parallels in the Noble Book, such as His saying, Exalted is He: «يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير».
And the poet's saying:
قالوا خراسان أقصى ما يراد بنا ... ثم القفول فقد جئنا خراسانا
(They said: Khurāsān is the farthest we are meant to go, then the return. Well, we have reached Khurāsān.)
i.e. this land is the farthest we are meant to go and the end of our journey, after which comes the return and going back. His saying «فقد جئنا» is consequent upon an omitted [element], i.e. if they spoke the truth, then we have reached Khurāsān, so why have we not been released from travel? It may also be that he turned to address, i.e. "so say to them: end the journey with us and return, for we have reached the appointed place."
(قد) is a particle of verification; (كذبوكم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (بما) is attached to (كذبوكم) and the clause (تقولون) is the ṣila. The wāw [of كذبوكم] applies to those worshipped and the kāf to the worshippers. (فما): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (ما) negative; (تستطيعون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (صرفا), i.e. warding off the punishment from you, is the direct object; and (ولا نصرا) is conjoined to (صرفا).
(وَمَنْ يَظْلِمْ مِنْكُمْ نُذِقْهُ عَذاباً كَبِيراً) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional noun that makes jussive, a mubtadaʾ; (يظلم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (منكم) is a ḥāl, i.e. being among you, O you who are legally responsible; (نذقه) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the verb and its apodosis are the khabar of (من). The hāʾ is the first object of (نذقه), (عذابا) the second object of (نذقه), and (كبيرا) an adjective.

dervis-irab:20-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِجْراً مَحْجُوراً): Sībawayh mentioned them in the chapter on non-inflecting maṣdars (verbal nouns) made accusative by verbs whose overt expression has been abandoned, such as «معاذ الله», «قعدك الله» and «عمرك الله». This is a word they used to utter on meeting a vengeful enemy, or at the onslaught of a calamity, or the like, putting it in the place of seeking refuge. Sībawayh said: "A man says to another:
'Will you do such-and-such?' and he says: 'ḥijran' — and it is from ḥajarahu, when he prevented him; because one who seeks refuge in Allah asks Him to prevent the hateful thing so that it does not reach him; so it is as if the meaning were: I ask Allah to prevent that with a prevention and to bar it with a barring."
Al-Zamakhsharī raised a question and said: "Since it has been established that it is of the category of maṣdars, what is the meaning of describing it as (محجور)? I say: this adjective came to emphasise the meaning of al-ḥijr, as they said «ذيل زائل» [Translator's note: so in the source; the known expression is «ذَيْلٌ ذائلٌ»] — and al-dhayl is abasement — and «موت مائت»." Al-ḥijr is [also] reason, because it restrains its owner. In al-Asās: "In that is a lesson for one with ḥijr, which is understanding; this is ḥijr upon you: forbidden; the judge placed him under interdiction (ḥajara ʿalayhi ḥajran); we drew water from al-ḥājir, which is a depression that holds water; so-and-so is of the people of al-Ḥājir, which is a place on the road to Mecca; he sat ḥajratan, i.e. aside; they surrounded the two ḥajratān of the army, which are its two flanks; he cauterised (ḥajjara) around the eye with a brand; 'I seek refuge in Allah, and ḥijr'; a woman white of the eye-sockets (maḥājir); her eye-socket (maḥjar) appeared from the veil; the clay became stony (istaḥjara) and hardened (taḥajjara): it became hard like stone; and he narrowed (taḥajjara) what Allah made wide: he made it narrow for himself." The reading of the majority is with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and it was read with ḍamma, which is a dialectal form of it. Abū al-Baqāʾ related a third form, which is fatḥa, and said it was read with it.
(هَباءً): Al-habāʾ — he said in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "dust and fine particles of earth, rising and scattered over the face of the earth; and people of little intelligence; its verb is habā yahbū hubuwwan." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-habāʾ is what comes out of a window-opening with the sunlight, resembling dust; among their proverbs: 'more insignificant than habāʾ'." He said: "The lām [final radical] of habāʾ is wāw, as evidenced by al-habwa." I say: al-Mutanabbī said:
ولا تحسبن المجد زقا وقينة ... فما المجد الا السيف والفتكة البكر
وتضريب أعناق الملوك وأن ترى ... لك الهبوات السود والعسكر المجر
(Do not think glory is a wineskin and a singing-girl; glory is nothing but the sword and the unprecedented bold strike, the striking of kings' necks, and that you see the black dust-clouds (habawāt) raised for you and the vast army.)
Al-Khalīl and al-Zajjāj said: "It is like the dust that enters the window-opening, appearing in the sunlight."

* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ وَيَمْشُونَ فِي الْأَسْواقِ) A resumptive clause set out to console him ﷺ. (ما) is negative; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (قبلك) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (من المرسلين) is attached to (أرسلنا), or to an omitted adjective of the object of (أرسلنا). The meaning is: "We did not send before you anyone of the messengers"; similar is His saying, Exalted is He, «وَما مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ», in the sense of "there is not one of us…"; and perhaps this is better. (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause (إنهم) is a ḥāl, and for that reason the hamza of (إن) was given kasra — just as it was given kasra because of the lām in the khabar (predicate). The meaning is "except while they ate", so the exception is from the most general of states. Inna and its noun; and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), which is the lām of inception shifted to the khabar; the clause (يأكلون الطعام) is the khabar of (إنهم), and the clause (يمشون في الأسواق) is conjoined to (ليأكلون الطعام). (وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ وَكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيراً) (وجعلنا) is conjoined to what preceded, or you may make it resumptive, also set out to console him ﷺ. (جعلنا) is a verb and its agent; (بعضكم) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لبعض) is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of (فتنة); and (فتنة) is the second direct object of (جعلنا). The meaning of making some of them a trial for others is that the rich is a trial for the poor, the healthy a trial for the sick, and the noble a trial for the lowly. What is meant is that this world is an abode of testing and affliction, so let that not blunt your resolve, nor let your breast be constricted by it, and pay no heed to their rumours [Translator's note: the source prints «الأراجيفهم», evidently for «لأراجيفهم»]. The hamza is for the interrogative, and the meaning of the interrogative is command, i.e. "be patient"; similar is «أأسلمتم», whose meaning is "submit". (وكان): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (كان) is a defective past verb; (ربك) is its noun and (بصيرا) its khabar. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْمَلائِكَةُ أَوْ نَرى رَبَّنا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (لا يرجون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لقاءنا) is the direct object. (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (أنزل) is a passive past verb; (علينا) is attached to it; (الملائكة) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause is the object of their speech — they are the ones who deny the resurrection. (أو) is a conjunction, and the clause (نرى ربنا) is conjoined to the clause (أنزل علينا الملائكة), so it is part of their speech. They proposed that Allah send down the angels upon them to inform them of Muḥammad's truthfulness so that they would believe him, or that they see Allah openly so that He would command them to believe him and follow him. (لَقَدِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَعَتَوْا عُتُوًّا كَبِيراً) The clause is the object of the speech of Allah the Exalted in repelling the two specious arguments which they put forward out of obstinacy and arrogance, after the proof had been established and the evidence had shone forth. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (استكبروا) is a verb and its agent. In (في أنفسهم) there are two views. The first is that it is attached to (استكبروا), meaning that, because of their arrogance, they considered themselves great (istakbarū anfusahum), i.e. counted them of great standing — its origin is from «استكبره», when he considered him great — and it was treated as an intransitive. The second is that it is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. they harboured arrogance against the truth in their hearts, i.e. [the arrogance] being in their hearts. (عتوا) is a past verb and its agent; (عتوا) [the noun] is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (كبيرا) its adjective. (يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ الْمَلائِكَةَ لا بُشْرى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَحْجُوراً) (يوم) is attached to an implied «اذكر», or to «يعذبون» (they are punished), or to «لا يبشرون» (they are given no glad tidings), understood implicitly from (لا بشرى), i.e. on the day they see the angels they are denied glad tidings or deprived of them. (البشرى) does not govern it, because the maṣdar does not govern what precedes it, and because what is negated does not govern what comes before (لا). The clause (يرون) is genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الملائكة) is the direct object. (لا بشرى): (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (بشرى) its noun and (للمجرمين) its khabar; the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "they say: no glad tidings", and the clause of saying is a ḥāl of (الملائكة). (يقولون) is a verb and its agent; and (حجرا محجورا) — the discussion of its parsing has preceded in detail in the section on vocabulary. (وَقَدِمْنا إِلى ما عَمِلُوا مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنْثُوراً) The wāw is resumptive; (قدمنا) is a verb and its agent; (إلى ما) is attached to (قدمنا); the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila; (من عمل) is a ḥāl, i.e. a good deed such as charity, maintaining kinship ties, or helping one in distress. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (جعلناه) is a verb, its agent and its first direct object; (هباء) is the second direct object and (منثورا) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
He likened the good deeds of the disbelievers to habāʾ (motes of dust). The point of resemblance is its littleness and insignificance, and its non-existence [Translator's note: the source prints «وعنده», evidently for «وعدمه»], and that no benefit is derived from it. Then, what kind of habāʾ? It may be ordered [in a line] with the sunlight, but when the wind stirs it, it flies about and goes in every direction. Therefore He said (منثورا), i.e. combining the insignificance of habāʾ with scattering. Similar is «كونوا قردة خاسئين», i.e. combining transformation and abasement. He brought the doer [Translator's note: so in the source, «بالعامل»; perhaps «بالعمل», "the deed", which is indefinite in «من عمل»] indefinite so that this threat would cover everyone whose soul entices him to remain in disbelief and do the like of their deeds.
Al-Rummānī, in his book al-Nukat fī Iʿjāz al-Qur'an, has a fine discussion of this simile, after placing it under the category of metaphor, in which he says: "The literal meaning of «قدمنا» here is «عمدنا» (We turned to/intended); and «قدمنا» is more eloquent than it, because it indicates that He treated them as one arriving from a journey does — since, by His granting them respite, He treated them as one absent from them who then arrives and sees them in a state contrary to [what he expected]. In this is a warning against being deceived by respite [Translator's note: the source prints «بالافهام», evidently for «بالإمهال», "respite"]. The meaning that unites them is justice, because intending to nullify what is corrupt is justice, and arriving to nullify what is corrupt is justice, and arriving is more eloquent for the reason we have explained. As for «هباء منثورا», it is an explanation that has brought out what the senses do not perceive into what they do perceive."
See how he gathered the Qur'anic images in his mind, how the word «قدمنا», borrowed from [other] meanings, inspired him, and then how he uncovered the hidden aspects of the Qur'anic expression in borrowing "arrival" for "intending", and the superiority of the former in stirring and arousing the imagination so as to link the first meaning in the verse with the borrowed meaning — and another linking image that arises in the imagination: the image of the absent traveller who comes and sees the people in discord, so he strikes in order to set things right and repair what is corrupt.
Al-Wāḥidī said: "The meaning of «قدمنا» is 'We turned to and intended'. It is said 'qadima fulān ilā amri kadhā' when he intended it or turned to it. Of this is the poet's saying:
وقدم الخوارج الضلال ... إلى عباد ربهم فقالوا
إن دماءكم لنا حلال
(The misguided Khawārij went to the servants of their Lord and said: your blood is lawful for us.)"
[Volume Seven]
[Continuation of Sūrat al-Furqān]

dervis-irab:24-29.t:
* I'rab:
(أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا) (أصحاب) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الجنة) the muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: the source says «مضاف»; (الجنة) is the muḍāf ilayhi]; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to one like it, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير); (خير) is the khabar (predicate) of (أصحاب), and it is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl), or [used] for mere description. (مستقرا) is a tamyīz (specification), and (أحسن مقيلا) is conjoined to (خير مستقرا). Al-mustaqarr is the place in which they spend most of their time [Translator's note: the source prints «الذين» for «الذي»], and al-maqīl is the place to which they retire to rest with their spouses and enjoy flirting with them. Further discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ بِالْغَمامِ وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلائِكَةُ تَنْزِيلًا) The adverb is accusative by an implied «اذكر» (remember); the clause (تشقق) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The origin of (تشقق) is (تتشقق): some readers dropped the [second] tāʾ and some assimilated it. (السماء) is the fāʿil (agent). (بالغمام): in this bāʾ there are several views. The first is that it is causal, meaning that it is split open because of its [the cloud's] emerging from it, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تشقق). The second is that it is of accompaniment (mulābasa), so the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The third is that it has the meaning of «عن», i.e. "from the clouds", as in His saying «يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم»; so it is also attached to (تتشقق). (نزل الملائكة): a passive past verb, (الملائكة) being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (تنزيلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَكانَ يَوْماً عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ عَسِيراً) (الملك) is the mubtadaʾ; the adverb is attached to it; (الحق) is an adjective of (الملك); and (للرحمن) is the khabar of (الملك). Some parsers permitted the adverb to be the khabar, and others permitted (الحق) to be; what we have mentioned is better. (وكان): the wāw is resumptive; (كان) is a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "and the day was"; (يوما) is its khabar; (على الكافرين) is attached to (عسيرا), and (عسيرا) is an adjective of (يوما). (وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ) The adverb is accusative by an implied «اذكر», and it is conjoined to His saying «يوم يرون الملائكة», as is His earlier saying «يوم تشقق السماء». The clause (يعض) is genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الظالم) is the fāʿil of (يعض); and (على يديه) is attached to (يعض) [Translator's note: the source prints «ببعض» for «بيعض»]. The meaning of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric. (يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا) The clause is accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of (يعض), i.e. "saying". (يا ليتني): (يا) is a vocative particle and the one addressed is omitted, or it is merely for drawing attention. (ليتني): layta and its noun, and the clause (اتخذت) is its khabar; (مع الرسول) is an adverb of place in the position of the second object of (اتخذت), and (سبيلا) is the first object of (اتخذت). He wishes he had accompanied the Messenger and followed the path of truth. (يا وَيْلَتى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلاناً خَلِيلًا) (يا) is a vocative particle and (ويلتا) is the one addressed, annexed to the yāʾ of the first person which has been turned into an alif [Translator's note: the source prints «الفاء» for «ألفا»]; its origin is «يا ويلتي» [Translator's note: the source prints «يا وليتي»]. The discussion of the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person has preceded. He calls out to his woe (waylatahu), i.e. his destruction. (ليتني): layta and its noun; the clause (لم أتخذ) is its khabar; (فلانا) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (خليلا) the second direct object. (لَقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ الذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ جاءَنِي وَكانَ الشَّيْطانُ لِلْإِنْسانِ خَذُولًا) The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (أضلني) is a verb and a latent agent [and the object]; (عن الذكر) is attached to (أضلني); and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for his aforementioned wish and his calling out to his destruction. (بعد) is an adverb annexed to one like it, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause (جاءني) is genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The wāw is circumstantial; (كان الشيطان) is kāna and its noun; (للإنسان) is attached to (خذولا); and (خذولا) is the khabar of kāna.

* Rhetoric:
The metonymy (kināya) is in His saying «مستقر» and «مقيل». As for al-mustaqarr, it is a noun of place from al-istiqrār (settling); it is the permanent sitting-place of the people of Paradise in which they settle and spend most of their time facing one another, conversing and talking at night. By it He alluded to the conversations of the evenings and mornings which they exchange — conversations that in this world went on among the affluent and the people of luxury and ease. And by al-maqīl, which is the time of midday rest, He alluded to their spending the time of leisure and rest with their spouses. In this sense will come His saying «إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون، هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون» [Translator's note: the source prints «هم أزواجهم»]. It has been said in explaining "the occupation" (al-shughl) that it is the deflowering of virgins.
Among the marvels of ḥadīth describing the singing of the ḥūr al-ʿīn is his saying ﷺ, in what Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrates from him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The wives of the people of Paradise sing to their husbands with the most beautiful voices anyone has ever heard. Among what they sing is: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, wives of a noble people, who look with delighted eyes.' And among what they sing is: 'We are the everlasting ones who do not die; we are the secure ones who do not fear; we are the abiding ones who do not depart.'"
In His saying «يوم يعض الظالم على يديه» there is a metonymy for regret, rage and sorrow. Like this expression are "biting the fingertips", "falling in the hand" (al-suqūṭ fī al-yad) and "grinding the molars" (ḥarq al-uram). In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "ḥaraqtu al-shayʾa ḥarqan: I filed it and rubbed parts of it against each other"; from it is their saying "ḥaraqa nābahu", i.e. he ground it until a grating sound was heard from it; and "so-and-so grinds his uram against you in rage", from "arama ʿalā al-shayʾ", i.e. he bit on it, and also "aramahu"; al-uram are the molars, as though it were the plural of ārim. It is said "so-and-so grinds his uram against you" when he is enraged and rubs his molars against each other. It is also said that it is a figure expressing perplexity, grief, regret and anguish. The authorities on language report that one who is sorrowful, grieving and regretful bites his thumb in regret. The poet said:
لطمت خدها بحمر لطاف ... نلن منها عذاب بيض عذاب
فشكى العناب نور أقاح ... واشتكى الورد ناضر العناب
(She slapped her cheek with delicate red [fingertips], which then took from her sweet white teeth [a bite]; so the jujube [fingertips] complained of the camomile blossom [teeth], and the rose [cheek] complained of the fresh jujube.)
(فلان) is an allusive word for a proper name of a rational being; (فل) is an allusive word for an indefinite rational male; (فلانة) is an allusive word for a proper name of a rational female; and (فلة) is an allusive word for an indefinite rational female. (الفلان) and (الفلانة), with the alif-lām, are allusive words for non-rational beings. Its lām [final radical] is wāw or yāʾ.
Abū Ḥayyān said: (فلان) is an allusive word for a proper name, and it is declinable (mutaṣarrif); (فل) is an allusive word for an indefinite human being, as in "O man!", and it is restricted to the vocative; and (فلة), meaning "O woman!", likewise. The lām of (فل) is yāʾ or wāw, and it is not a truncated (murakhkham) form of (فلان), contrary to al-Farrāʾ. Ibn ʿUṣfūr, Ibn Mālik and the author of al-Basīṭ erred in saying that (فل) is an allusive word for a proper name, like (فلان); and in the Book of Sībawayh there is what we have said, transmitted from the Arabs.

dervis-irab:50-57.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ): He made them adjacent and touching one another, such that they do not mix. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-marj is land with vegetation and pasture; the plural is murūj, like falus and fulūs. You say marajat al-dābba marjan (from the pattern of qatala) when the animal grazed in the meadow, and marajtuhā marjan when I let it loose to graze in the meadow." In al-Mukhtār: and His saying, the Exalted, «مرج البحرين» means He left them alone, so that neither is confused with the other. In al-Asās: "amraja al-dawābba and marrajahā: he let them loose in the meadow and the meadows; marajā al-sulṭān al-nās (the ruler left the people unrestrained); a rajul mārij is one let loose, not restrained; so-and-so keeps on marjan upon us, murūjan: he keeps coming to us suddenly; marija the ring on the finger: it was loose. And figuratively: «marraja Allāh al-baḥrayn», and so-and-so marraja his tongue against people's honour, and amrajahu; so-and-so is sarrāj marrāj: a liar; their covenants became unsettled (marijat) and their affair became disordered (marija amruhum marjan wa murūjan), and an amr mārij and marīj; and in the ḥadīth: «How will you be when religion becomes disordered (marija) and avarice appears?» Zuhayr said:
(Verse in Arabic:) مرج الدين فأعددت له ... مشرف الحارك محبوك الثبج
يرهب السوط سريعا فإذا ... ونت الخيل من الشد معج
(Gloss: "Religion became disordered, so I prepared for it a horse with a high withers and a well-knit back; it fears the whip and is swift, and when the horses grow slack from galloping, it races on.")
They amrajū their covenants and their religion; and a mārij of fire rose: a towering flame." [Translator's note: this passage is quoted from al-Asās as it stands in the source; the sentence beginning "And figuratively" appears there as written.]
Furthermore, a great quantity of water is called a "sea" (baḥr), without a pair of specific seas being intended.
(فُراتٌ): al-furāt is what is extremely sweet, to the point of bordering on sugary-sweet. The tāʾ in it is radical, being the lām of the word, and its pattern is fiʿāl. Some Arabs pause on it with a hāʾ. It is said that sweet water was called furāt because it "furrows" (yafrut) thirst, that is, splits and cuts it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-furāt is sweet water; one says farata al-māʾ furūtatan (on the pattern of sahula suhūlatan) when it became sweet; it is pluralised only rarely, as furtān, like ghurbān." Al-Furāt is also a famous great river, and al-furāt is also the sea.
(أُجاجٌ): al-ujāj is what is extreme in saltiness; it is also said, in heat, and also said, in bitterness. In al-Asās: "māʾ ujāj: it burns with its saltiness." In al-Qāmūs: "ajja yaujju al-māʾ: the water became ujāj, that is, salty and bitter." Here is a linguistic digest detailing the quantity and quality of water: if water is permanent, never ceasing and not drained, in a spring or a well, it is ʿadd; if, when one side of it is stirred, its other side is not disturbed, it is kurr; if it is plentiful and sweet, it is ghadaq, and the Qur'an has spoken of it; if it is overflowing, it is ghamr; if it is beneath the ground, it is ghawr; if it is flowing, it is ghayl; if it is on the surface of the earth and is drawn without a device, it is sayḥ; if it is manifest, flowing over the face of the earth, it is maʿīn and sanam, and in the ḥadīth: «The best water is the sanam»; if it is flowing among trees, it is ghalal; if it is standing in a pit or a hollow, it is thaghab; if it is drawn out of a well, it is nabaṭ; if a flood leaves a portion of it behind, it is ghadīr; if it reaches the ankles or half the shins, it is ḍaḥḍāḥ; if it is near the bottom, it is ḍaḥl; if animals have waded through it and changed it, it is ṭaraq; if it is stinking but drinkable, it is ājin, otherwise it is āsin; if it is cold and stinking, it is ghassāq; or if it is hot, then it is heated (sakhin); if its heat intensifies, it is ḥamīm; if it is salty, it is zuʿāq; or bitter, it is qaʿāʿ; if saltiness and bitterness are combined in it, it is ujāj; if it has some sweetness and people may drink it despite what is in it, it is sharīb; if it is lower than that in sweetness and people drink it only out of necessity while cattle may drink it, it is shurūb; if it is sweet, it is furāt; if its sweetness increases, it is nuqākh; if it is wholesome for livestock, it is namīr; if it is easy, pleasant and flows smoothly down the throat, it is salsal and salsāl; if it combines clarity, sweetness and coolness, it is zulāl; if people crowd over it so much that they drain it with their lips, it is mashfūh, then mathmūd, then maḍfūf, then mamkūl, then majmūm, then manqūṣ." How wondrous is the matter of our noble language!
(بَرْزَخاً): a barrier that prevents either of them from mixing with the other, without being seen.
(وَحِجْراً مَحْجُوراً): their explanation has already been given, and the discussion of their position here will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَصِهْراً): al-ṣihr, with a kasra, is kinship, as in al-Qāmūs, and also the son-in-law (khatan); its plural is aṣhār [Translator's note: the source prints "جعمه", an evident misprint for "جمعه" (its plural)]. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-ṣihr; its plural is aṣhār. Al-Khalīl said: al-ṣihr is the family of the woman's household; and he said: some of the Arabs make both the aḥmāʾ (the husband's relatives) and the akhtān (the wife's relatives) all aṣhār. Al-Azharī said: al-ṣihr includes the women's relatives who are within the prohibited degrees, male and female, such as parents, siblings and their children, paternal uncles, maternal uncles and maternal aunts; these are the in-laws of the woman's husband, and whoever is on the husband's side of his relatives within the prohibited degrees are likewise the in-laws of the wife. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: everyone on the husband's side, his father, brother or paternal uncle, they are the aḥmāʾ, and whoever is on the woman's side, they are the akhtān, and both categories are combined under aṣhār. You say ṣāhartu ilayhim, lahum and fīhim when you have married from among them."
(ظَهِيراً): al-ẓahīr is the helper; it is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of mufāʿil. It is also permissible that al-ẓahīr be meant as a group, as in His saying «والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير», just as ṣadīq and khalīṭ have come (used for the plural).

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْناهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُوراً): conjoined to what precedes. The lām is the lām of the response to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of affirmation; «صرفناه» is a verb, agent and direct object. The pronoun refers to the water, or to the statement that has already mentioned the bringing forth of the clouds and the sending down of rain among people so that they might take heed, but they refused except ingratitude. «بينهم» is attached to «صرفناه». «ليذكروا»: the lām is for purpose, and «يذكروا» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied an after the lām. «فأبى أكثر الناس»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. «إلا» is a particle of restriction, and «كفورا» is a direct object or an absolute object.
(وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَبَعَثْنا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَذِيراً): the wāw is a conjunction; «لو» is conditional; «شئنا» is a verb and agent, and the object of the willing is omitted, and it has already been mentioned that this is frequent after a verb of willing. The lām falls in the response to «لو», and the clause «بعثنا» has no grammatical position. «في كل قرية» is a preposition phrase attached to «بعثنا», and «نذيرا» is a direct object. The meaning is: but We confined the matter to you and entrusted it to you alone, so that you might have the merit of manifesting it and the practice of bearing its burdens.
(فَلا تُطِعِ الْكافِرِينَ وَجاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهاداً كَبِيراً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); «لا» is prohibitive; «تطع» is jussive by lā, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «الكافرين» is a direct object, meaning: do not go along with them in what they want from you, and let no leniency take hold of you with them. «جاهدهم» is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «به» is attached to «جاهدهم», and the pronoun refers to the Qur'an: recite to them constantly its prohibitions, its commands and its warnings. «جهادا» is an absolute object and «كبيرا» an adjective.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هذا عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ وَهذا مِلْحٌ أُجاجٌ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the discourse is conjoined to what precedes so that the mention of the five proofs of His oneness proceeds in harmony; this is the fourth proof. «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «مرج البحرين» is the ṣila. The clause «هذا عذب» is resumptive, or it is a quotation of an omitted saying, in the position of ḥāl, that is, "it being said of them both". «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «عذب» its khabar, and «فرات» a second khabar. «وهذا ملح أجاج» is conjoined to what precedes.
(وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخاً وَحِجْراً مَحْجُوراً): conjoined to «مرج», falling within the scope of the ṣila. «جعل» is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; «بينهما» is an adverbial attached to an omitted element, in the position of the second object of «جعل»; «برزخا» is the first direct object; «حجرا محجورا» is conjoined to «برزخا». It has also been said that the two are accusative through an implied saying; the elaboration of that will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْماءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً وَكانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيراً): conjoined to what precedes; the fifth proof is mentioned in it. «من الماء» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خلق», and «بشرا» is a direct object. «فجعله»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «جعله» is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; «نسبا» is a second object; «صهرا» is conjoined to «نسبا». The wāw is resumptive; «كان» is a defective past verb, «ربك» its noun, and «قديرا» its khabar.
(وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَلا يَضُرُّهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause «يعبدون» is resumptive, introduced to begin denouncing the idolaters' inclination to worship idols after the five proofs of oneness have been given. «من دون الله» is a ḥāl; «ما» is a direct object; the clause «لا ينفعهم» is the ṣila; and the clause «ولا يضرهم» is conjoined to the clause «لا ينفعهم».
(وَكانَ الْكافِرُ عَلى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً): the wāw is a conjunction. «كان الكافر»: kāna and its noun; «على ربه» is attached to «ظهيرا», and «ظهيرا» is the khabar of kāna, that is, a helper of Satan.
(وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً): resumptive discourse, introduced to affirm the state of His Messenger ﷺ. «ما» is negative; «أرسلناك» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «مبشرا» is a ḥāl, so the exception is from the most general of circumstances; «نذيرا» is conjoined to «مبشرا».
(قُلْ ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ): «قل» is an imperative verb, and the clause «ما أسألكم» is the content of the saying. «عليه» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «أجر» and was put before it. «من» is a redundant preposition, and «أجر» is genitive in form, in the position of the accusative as direct object of «أسألكم».
(إِلَّا مَنْ شاءَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا): «إلا» is a particle of exception; «من شاء» is a disconnected exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), because it is not of the same kind, that is: I ask no wage from you for myself, but whoever wishes to spend his wealth in the path of Allah, purely for His countenance, let him do so. «أن» and what is within its scope is the object of the willing; «إلى ربه» is in the position of the second object of «يتخذ», and «سبيلا» is the first direct object of «يتخذ».

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya) in His saying «مرج البحرين»: He likened by the two the two abundant, vast bodies of water. «حجرا محجورا» is a phrase said when seeking refuge, as we mentioned earlier in this sura, but here the two are said figuratively, as if each of the two seas seeks refuge from the other and says to it «حجرا محجورا». So parsing «حجرا محجورا» as two objects of the omitted saying is exceedingly good from the standpoint of bayān. His saying «بينهما برزخ لا يبغيان» will come in Sūrat al-Raḥmān, where He likened them, as we said, to two hostile parties, each wishing to strike the other, lying in wait for it for misfortunes and seizing chances and opportunities, yet when it gets what it wants it refrains from transgression. So the metaphorical meaning was made like a spoken utterance, and this is among the most eloquent of speech, the clearest, the most vivid and the most suited to the intended meaning.

dervis-irab:58-60.t:
* I'rab:
(وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction on what precedes, and the verse is connected with His saying «وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا», for when He made clear that the disbelievers back one another in harming him, He commanded him to put his trust in Him. «توكل» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «على الحي» is a preposition phrase attached to «توكل»; «الذي» is an adjective, and the clause «لا يموت» is the ṣila. «سبح» is conjoined to «توكل», and «بحمده» is a preposition phrase attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, that is, "engaged in praising Him".
(وَكَفى بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبادِهِ خَبِيراً): the wāw is a conjunction; «كفى» is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and the hāʾ is genitive in form and nominative in position, as the agent. «بذنوب» is a preposition phrase attached to «خبيرا», and «خبيرا» is a tamyīz (specification) or a ḥāl.
(الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ): «الذي» is an adjective or a badal (substitute) of «به», or a mubtadaʾ; the clause «خلق السموات والأرض» is the ṣila; «وما بينهما» is conjoined to «السموات», and the adverbial is attached to an omitted element forming the ṣila; «في ستة أيام» is a preposition phrase attached to «خلق».
(ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ الرَّحْمنُ فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً): «ثم» is a conjunction; «استوى» is conjoined to «خلق»; «على العرش» is a preposition phrase attached to it; «الرحمن» is the khabar of «الذي», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is al-Raḥmān". «فاسأل»: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and «اسأل» is an imperative verb; «به» is a preposition phrase attached to «خبيرا», and «خبيرا» is a direct object. It is also permissible that the bāʾ be in the sense of ʿan (about), the preposition phrase being attached to His saying «فاسأل». Among such usage is the poet's saying:
فإن تسألوني بالنساء فإنني ... خبير بأدواء النساء طبيب
(Gloss: "If you ask me about women, I am well-versed in the ailments of women, a physician.")
and the saying of ʿAntara:
هلا سألت الخيل يا ابنة مالك ... إن كنت جاهلة بما لم تعلمي
(Gloss: "Why did you not ask the horsemen, daughter of Mālik, if you are ignorant of what you do not know?")
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمنِ قالُوا وَمَا الرَّحْمنُ): the wāw is resumptive; «إذا» is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause «قيل» is genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; «لهم» is attached to «قيل»; the clause «اسجدوا للرحمن» is the content of the saying; the clause «قالوا» is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. The wāw (in «وما») is redundant; «ما الرحمن»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar, and «الرحمن» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, or the reverse. It is permissible that it be a question about the one so named or about its meaning.
(أَنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا وَزادَهُمْ نُفُوراً): the hamza is for rhetorical (denunciatory) interrogation; «نسجد» is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; «لما» is attached to «نسجد», that is: how can we prostrate to what we do not know? The clause «تأمرنا» is the ṣila. It is permissible that «ما» be maṣdar (verbal-noun forming), that is, "do we prostrate because of your command?" «زادهم» is a verb and agent, the agent referring to the saying, and the hāʾ is a direct object; «نفورا» is a second direct object or a tamyīz.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ثم استوى على العرش» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), which the early scholars call takhyīliyya (imaginative). The thing borrowed is istiwāʾ (settling, being level); the source of the borrowing is every level body; the one to whom it is lent is the Truth, Mighty and Majestic. This is so that the hearer, on hearing this word, imagines a king who has finished arranging his realms and consolidating his kingdom and everything his subjects and troops need, the building up of his lands and the management of his servants' affairs, and has settled on the throne of his kingship in a settling of grandeur. Thus on hearing this speech the hearer measures what is hidden from his perception of the matter of divinity against what he imagines of the matter of worldly kingship. For this reason the mention of istiwāʾ on the Throne never occurs except after the report of having finished the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, even though there is no throne set up, no perceptible sitting, and no settling in the sense indicated by the outward meaning, namely a specific posture.

Benefit:
There are two schools on istiwāʾ. The first is the school of the Salaf, which does not interpret istiwāʾ but says that it is an istiwāʾ befitting Him. The second is the school of the Khalaf, which interprets it as having mastery over it, by exercising control over it and over the rest of creation.

* Benefits:
His saying «في ستة أيام»: that is, in the measure of this period. The apparent sense is that they are of the days of this world, the first being Sunday and the last Friday. They had names for them among the Arabs, namely: al-Aḥad: Awhal; al-Ithnayn: Awhan; al-Thulāthāʾ: Jubār; al-Arbiʿāʾ: Dubār; al-Khamīs: Muʾnis; al-Jumuʿa: ʿArūba; al-Sabt: Shiyār.

dervis-irab:61-66.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُرُوجاً): that is, the mansions of the planets, which are twelve. The original meaning of burūj is lofty palaces; these mansions were called burūj because for the planets they are like the lofty dwellings, which are palaces, for their inhabitants. Now, the zodiacal belt is a celestial belt containing the orbits traversed by the planets around the sun, and the inclination of these orbits relative to one another differs in being small or large, particularly the orbits of the planets that are seen only with a great astronomical instrument. This belt is divided by the ecliptic circle, called the orbit of the earth, into two equal halves, the width of each being approximately eight degrees, and they end in two circles parallel to that circle; it is inclined away from the equatorial circle, which divides it into two nearly equal halves. In past ages it was divided into twelve parts called ṣuwar (figures), each part being thirty degrees. From the apparent course of the sun through these parts the seasons and their durations arise. That is, this star, by leaving the southern half of the sphere and entering its northern half, opens the solar year, I mean the moment it enters the sign of Aries; at that time spring begins, by which the universe comes to life, and this season continues for the period of the sun's passage through the said sign and the signs of Taurus and Gemini.
