Then it enters in succession Cancer, Leo and Virgo, and these are called the season of summer; during its stay in those signs intensely hot rays are sent to us which ripen the grain that is harvested in summer. Then, after reaching this height, it descends from the side of the southern half and passes in turn through Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius; these three signs are called the season of autumn. Then winter enters with its snow and cold, the sun then being at the farthest point from us and sending to us only slanting rays; it traverses its three signs, I mean Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces, and then returns to its first place to restore life and movement to many of the beings that had been as if void of them because of its distance from them.
You have thus learned that the twelve figures of the zodiacal belt are divided among the four seasons: for spring, Aries, Taurus and Gemini; for summer, Cancer, Leo and Virgo; for autumn, Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius; and for winter, Capricorn, the Water-Pourer (Aquarius) and Pisces.
(سِراجاً): al-sirāj is the sun, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وجعل الشمس سراجا».
(خِلْفَةً): that is, each of them succeeds the other; khilfa is a maṣdar of manner (maṣdar hayʾa).
The wording of al-Qurṭubī: Abū ʿUbayda said: al-khilfa is everything after something else, so each of night and day succeeds its fellow. One says of one who has diarrhoea: khilfa has befallen him, that is, standing and sitting, this one succeeding that one; from it comes khilfat al-nabāt, which is a leaf that comes out after the first leaf on the high ground. Mujāhid said: khilfa is from khilāf (difference): this one white and that one black; the first is stronger. It is also said that they alternate in light and darkness and in increase and decrease. It is also said that it is a case of omission of the muḍāf, that is, He made night and day possessors of khilfa, that is, of difference, for whoever wishes to remember, that is, to take heed, and so know that Allah did not make them so in vain, and so reflect on the works of Allah the Exalted and thank Allah for His favours to him in reason, thought and understanding. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan said: its meaning is that whoever misses something of good at night will catch it by day, and whoever misses it by day will catch it by night.
(هَوْناً): al-hawn is gentleness and calm. It is a maṣdar put in the place of an adjective for emphasis, and similar cases have already passed. From it is the ḥadīth: «Love your beloved moderately (hawnan mā)» and the saying «The believers are gentle (hayyinūn) and soft», and among their proverbs: «When your brother is mighty, be gentle (fahun)».
(غَراماً): destruction, loss and lasting punishment. In al-Mukhtār: "al-gharām: perpetual evil and punishment." Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim said:
ويوم النسار ويوم الفجا.... ركانا عذابا وكان غراما
(Gloss: "And the day of al-Nisār and the day of al-Jifār [the source prints al-Fajā in the verse]: they were for us a punishment and a perpetual ruin.") [Translator's note: the verse is quoted as printed in the source, with the odd word "ركانا"; the commentary that follows names the two places as al-Nisār and al-Fijār.] Al-Nisār is a water of Banū ʿĀmir and al-Fijār a water of Banū Tamīm; these two events took place at them, and they were a punishment for their people and perpetual destruction.

* I'rab:
(تَبارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّماءِ بُرُوجاً وَجَعَلَ فِيها سِراجاً وَقَمَراً مُنِيراً): «تبارك» is an indeclinable (jāmid) past verb; «الذي» is its agent; the clause «جعل» is the ṣila; «في السماء» is attached to «جعل»; «بروجا» is a direct object, and what follows is conjoined to it. It is permissible that «جعل» be transitive to two objects, in the sense of making, that is, turning into.
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرادَ شُكُوراً): discourse conjoined to what precedes. «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «جعل الليل والنهار» is the ṣila; «خلفة» is a second direct object of «جعل» if it is in the sense of "turned into", or a ḥāl if it is in the sense of "created". It is singular because the meaning is that one succeeds the other, and this is not realised except through the two together. It is said that an implied muḍāf is necessary, that is, "possessors of khilfa", as mentioned earlier under Vocabulary. «لمن» is an adjective of «خلفة»; the clause «أراد» is the ṣila of «من»; «أن يذكر» is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative as the object of «أراد», and the object of «يذكر» is omitted, that is, "what he missed in one of them". «أو» is a conjunction, and «أراد شكورا» is conjoined to the first «أراد».
(وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْناً): resumptive discourse, introduced to set out the qualities by which the sincere servants of al-Raḥmān are distinguished, after setting out the state of the hypocrites; He described them with eight relative nouns. «عباد» is a mubtadaʾ and «الرحمن» its muḍāf ilayhi, and what follows are adjectives. It is permissible that the eight relative nouns be descriptions, with the khabar of «عباد» at the end of the sura, namely His saying, the Exalted, «أولئك يجزون الغرفة», as if He had said: "the servants of al-Raḥmān who are described with these qualities, those are rewarded..." Perhaps the first is preferable because it is free of strain. «الذين» is the khabar of «عباد» or an adjective; the clause «يمشون» is the ṣila; «على الأرض» is attached to «يمشون»; and «هونا» is a maṣdar put in the position of a ḥāl, or accusative as an absolute object, as if it were a description of the maṣdar or of what coincides with it in meaning, that is, "a gentle walking".
(وَإِذا خاطَبَهُمُ الْجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلاماً): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, so it falls within the scope of the ṣila. «إذا» is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause «خاطبهم الجاهلون» is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause «قالوا» has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «سلاما» is an absolute object, that is, a saying in which they are safe from sin. An interesting discussion between Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad about this maṣdar will come in the section on Benefits.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِياماً): «والذين» is conjoined to the first relative noun; the clause «يبيتون» is the ṣila; the wāw is the noun of «يبيتون», and it is weak to make it a complete verb, that is, "they enter into the night-stay (bayāt)", as will come in the section on Benefits. «لربهم» is attached to «سجدا»; «سجدا» is the khabar of «يبيتون», or a ḥāl if it is taken as complete; «قياما» is conjoined to «سجدا». Prostration was put before standing, although standing precedes it in the act, out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil). «سجدا» is the plural of sājid, an active participle, and for that reason the preposition phrase is attached to it; likewise «قياما» is the plural of qāʾim.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذابَ جَهَنَّمَ): «والذين» is also conjoined; the clause «يقولون» is the ṣila; «ربنا» is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; «اصرف» is an imperative verb whose meaning is supplication; «عذاب جهنم» is the object of «اصرف», and the clause is the content of the saying.
(إِنَّ عَذابَها كانَ غَراماً): the clause is explanatory of cause and has no position, being the reason for their saying «ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم». «إن» and its noun; the clause «كان» is its khabar; the noun of «كان» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", and «غراما» is the khabar of «كان».
(إِنَّها ساءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقاماً): this clause is also explanatory of cause, the conjunction between them having been omitted, so the two clauses are part of what they say. «إن» and its noun; the clause «ساءت» is its khabar; the agent of «ساءت» is a latent vague pronoun explained by an indefinite noun; «مستقرا» is a tamyīz and «مقاما» is conjoined to «مستقرا»; the specified object of censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it". The parsers, such as al-Zamakhsharī and al-Samīn, have permitted «ساءت» to be in the sense of "grieved", in which case it is not among the verbs of censure but a fully conjugated verb governing a direct object, which here is omitted, that is, "and it grieved its inhabitants and those who enter it"; in that case «مستقرا» may be a tamyīz or a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
1- A discussion on «سلاما»:
Al-Qurṭubī said in his commentary: "Al-Naḥḥās said: we do not know of any statement of Sībawayh on the meaning of abrogating and abrogated except on this verse. Sībawayh said: the Muslims were not commanded on that day to greet the disbelievers with salām, rather it is in the sense of the saying 'we are safe from you; there is no good between us and you, and no evil.' Al-Mubarrad said: he should have said: the Muslims were not commanded on that day to fight them, then they were commanded to fight them. And he, that is Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad, said: Sībawayh erred in this and phrased it badly. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: the Muslims were not commanded on that day to greet the polytheists with salām, nor were they forbidden to do so; rather they were commanded to forgive and to shun them graciously. The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to stand at their gatherings, greet them and approach them, without flattering them."
I say: there is no need to claim abrogation, because turning away from the foolish and not returning like for like is commendable in manners, in manliness and in the Sharīʿa, and better protects honour and preserves it more fully.
2- The verb "bāta":
He said in al-Qāmūs: "bāta yafʿalu kadhā, yabītu and yabātu, baytan, bayātan, mabītan and baytūtatan: that is, he does it at night, and it is not from sleep." The meaning of "and it is not from sleep" is that the action is not sleeping: so if he slept at night it is not correct to say "bāta yanāmu". From it is the saying of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī:
أتبيت ريان الجفون من الكرى ... وأبيت منك بليلة الملسوع
(Gloss: "Do you spend the night with eyelids sated with sleep, while I spend the night, because of you, like the night of one stung?")
Ibn Hishām mentioned in Mughnī al-Labīb, from a great man among the jurists, that he found the above-mentioned saying of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī problematic, and said: "How is the tāʾ of «تبيت» given a ḍamma, though it is for the addressee and not the speaker, and the hamza-form of «أبيت», which is for the speaker, a fatḥa?" I explained to the narrator that both verbs are imperfect, that the tāʾ in both is the lām of the word (the root letter), that the address in the first is understood from the hamza (the interrogative), and that the first is nominative because it takes the place of a noun, while the second is accusative by an implied an after the wāw of accompaniment, as in the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
ألم أك جاركم ويكون بيني ... وبينكم المودة والإخاء
(Gloss: "Was I not your neighbour, and may there be between me and you affection and brotherhood?")
Now we return to the verse of al-Sharīf and say: it is among the most delicate and most beautiful poetry. It contains a derivative metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya), in that it likened the fullness of the beloved's eyelids with sleep to riyy (quenched thirst), which is the filling of the belly with water that removes the burning of thirst, on the ground of common attainment of ease in both; the name of the thing likened to was borrowed for the thing likened, and rayyān, meaning "one whose eyelids are full", was derived from riyy. It also contains a kināya (metonymy), for by "the night of the one stung" he alluded to the night of wakefulness, because wakefulness and sleeplessness are among its concomitants. It also contains a ṭibāq (antithesis) between sleep, understood explicitly from the first half, and wakefulness, understood by metonymy from the second half. The verse has thus completed three arts of bayān; and if you add to that the departure of the interrogative from its original meaning to confiding and complaint, it has completed four arts, to which a fifth is added, the art of fine arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq) and smoothness of style.
It belongs to verses from which we cite the following bouquet:
يا صاحب القلب الصحيح أما اشتفى ... ألم الجوى من قلبي المصدوع
(Gloss: "O you of the sound heart, has the pain of passion not been healed in my broken heart?")
هيهات لا تتكلفنّ لي الهوى ... فضح التطبع شيمة المطبوع
(Gloss: "Far from it; do not affect love for me; affectation is exposed by the natural disposition of one who is natural.")
كم قد نصبت لك الحبائل طامعا ... فنجوت بعد تعرض لوقوع
(Gloss: "How many snares I set for you, hoping, and you escaped after nearly falling.")
وتركتني ظمآن أشرب غلتي ... أسفا على ذاك اللمي الممنوع
(Gloss: "And you left me thirsty, drinking my own thirst in sorrow for that forbidden dark-lipped sweetness.")
كم ليلة جرّعتني في طولها ... غصص الملام ومؤلم التقريع
(Gloss: "How many a night, in its length, you made me swallow the chokings of blame and painful reproach.") [Translator's note: the source prints "جرّ عته"; "جرّعتني" is the evident sense.]
أبكي ويبسم والدجى ما بيننا ... حتى أضاء بثغره ودموعي
(Gloss: "I weep and he smiles, with the darkness between us, until it was lit by his mouth and my tears.")
قمر إذا استعجلته بعتابه ... لبس الغروب ولم يعد لطلوع
(Gloss: "A moon which, when you hurry it with reproach, puts on setting and does not return to rise.")
لو حيث يستمع السرار وفقتما ... لعجبتما من عزه وخضوعي
(Gloss: "If, where secrets are overheard, you two had been present, you would marvel at his pride and my submission.") [Translator's note: in the source this line is run together with the next on one line and the word "خضوعي" is broken as "وخ / ضوعي"; it has been restored here as the evident reading.]
أهون علي إذا امتلأت من الكرى ... أني أبيت بليلة الملسوع
(Gloss: "It is easier for me, when you are full of sleep, that I should spend the night like the night of one stung.")
[Translator's note: the final line is printed in the source beginning "ضوعي أهون علي ..." as a continuation of the broken word above.]
"Bāta" is complete (tāmm), being content with its nominative without its accusative, when it is in the sense of ʿarrasa, which is to alight at the end of the night, as in the saying of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: «As for the Messenger of Allah, he spent the night (bāta) at Minā», that is, he alighted there at night's end. Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀnis, with a nūn, who is other than Imruʾ al-Qays ibn Ḥujr al-Kindī, said:
وبات وباتت له ليلة ... كليلة ذي العائر الأرمد
(Gloss: "He spent the night, and for him there passed a night like the night of one with a mote in a sore, inflamed eye.")
that is, "and he alighted". Al-ʿāʾir, with the unpointed ʿayn, is an active participle from al-ʿawar, which is the speck in the eye at which it waters; it is also said to be ophthalmia, and al-armad is an adjective of it. They say "bāta bi-l-qawm", meaning he alighted among them at night.

dervis-irab:30-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَهْجُوراً): abandoned, i.e. they left it and turned away from believing in it. It is also said to be from هَجَرَ when he raves, i.e. "they made it something raved about", so the preposition was omitted. In this sense it admits two aspects: one, that they claimed it was raving, falsehood and fables of the ancients; the other, that when they heard it they would talk obscenely about it. It is then either from al-hajr with fatḥa, the opposite of joining, or from al-hujr with ḍamma, which is raving and foul speech. Further, al-mahjūr is either a passive participle or a maṣdar with the sense of al-hajr, applied to the Qur'an on the way of naming by a maṣdar, like al-majlūd, al-maʿqūl, al-maysūr and al-maʿsūr.
(وَرَتَّلْناهُ): We divided it up, or We brought it little by little, with deliberation and gentleness, in order to ease its understanding and memorisation. Its origin is tartīl in the teeth, which is their being spaced; one says thaghr murattal and ratil with two fatḥas.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ يا رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هذَا الْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً) It is conjoined to His saying وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا. قالَ الرَّسُولُ is a verb and an agent; يا is a particle of vocative; رَبِّ is a vocative annexed to the first-person yāʾ; إنّ and its noun; the clause اتَّخَذُوا is its khabar; هذا is the first object of اتَّخَذُوا; الْقُرْآنَ is a badal of the demonstrative; and مَهْجُوراً is the second direct object. (وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive and the speech is resumptive, brought to console him ﷺ after the distress he endures, which his bitter complaint indicates. وَكَذلِكَ is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "We made, a making like that"; لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ is the second object of جَعَلْنا; عَدُوًّا is the first direct object; and مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ is an adjective of عَدُوًّا.
(وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ هادِياً وَنَصِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction; كَفى is a past verb; بِرَبِّكَ: the bāʾ is a preposition redundant in the agent, and رَبِّكَ is genitive in wording, an agent of كَفى in position; هادِياً is a ḥāl and نَصِيراً is conjoined to it. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to relate a doubt of theirs concerning the Qur'an; those relating it are Quraysh or the Jews, and it is an objection that collapses and falls from its foundation, because the inimitability of the Qur'an is not tied to its being sent down all at once or in parts. قالَ الَّذِينَ is a verb and an agent; the clause كَفَرُوا is a ṣila; لَوْلا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); نُزِّلَ is a passive past verb; عَلَيْهِ is attached to نُزِّلَ; الْقُرْآنُ is the nāʾib fāʿil; جُمْلَةً is a ḥāl, and واحِدَةً an adjective. (كَذلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلًا) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "We sent it down, a sending down like that sending down"; لِنُثَبِّتَ is a purpose clause for the omitted "We sent it down"; بِهِ is attached to نُثَبِّتَ and the agent is latent, its implied form being "We"; فُؤادَكَ is a direct object; وَرَتَّلْناهُ is conjoined to the omitted "We sent it down", a past verb, an agent and a direct object; and تَرْتِيلًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. The meaning of its tartīl is that He measured it out verse after verse, with deliberation and steadiness; and it is said that it means He sent it down, though in parts, with lingering and gradualness over a distant span, which was twenty years.
(وَلا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْناكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يَأْتُونَكَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بِمَثَلٍ is attached to يَأْتُونَكَ, i.e. with a strange question that resembles in its oddity and falsity the current proverb; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; جِئْناكَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بِالْحَقِّ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جِئْناكَ; the exception is an emptied one (mufarragh) from the most general of states, so the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "they bring you no parable in any state except in the state of Our bringing you the truth and what is better in exposition". وَأَحْسَنَ is conjoined to الْحَقِّ and is genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, and تَفْسِيراً is a tamyīz. (الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلى جَهَنَّمَ) الَّذِينَ is nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they", or accusative in the sense of censure, i.e. "I censure those who"; the clause يُحْشَرُونَ is a ṣila; عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "turned over on their faces"; and إِلى جَهَنَّمَ is attached to يُحْشَرُونَ.
(أُوْلئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا) أُوْلئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ; شَرٌّ is a khabar; مَكاناً is a tamyīz; وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا is conjoined to شَرٌّ مَكاناً; and the clause is explicative and so has no position. You may also parse الَّذِينَ as a mubtadaʾ with the clause as its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The describing of the place as evil and the way as astray is of the figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī). Parallels to it have passed.
2- The strength of the wording for the strength of the meaning:
This is in His saying: «ورتلناه ترتيلا». The word rattala is on the pattern of qattala, the quadriliteral form, and yet it does not indicate abundance of reading; what is meant is that the reading be in a manner of deliberation and reflection. The reason is that this word has no triliteral from which it could be transferred to a quadriliteral; it is a quadriliteral set down for this specific fine manner of reading. For if the word were transferred, it would lead to abundance. Take as an example kallama in His saying «وكلّم الله موسى تكليما»: kallama is also on the pattern of qattala, and it is not meant to convey intensity but rather: He addressed him, whether His address to him was long or short, little or much; and this word is quadriliteral and has no triliteral from which it was transferred to the quadriliteral.
But the very same word has occurred with a triliteral and a quadriliteral, the quadriliteral being more frequent and stronger in the meaning it indicates, namely when kallama is from wounding, i.e. jarraḥa; it has a triliteral, kalama in the light form, meaning jaraḥa. When it occurs in the light form it indicates wounding once, and when it occurs in the heavy form it indicates intensity. Reflect on this, for it is very fine and few perceive it.
3- In His saying «ولا يأتونك بمثل» is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya). He likened the question to a parable, with the common ground being falsity, because most parables are imagined matters.

dervis-irab:67-71.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَقْتُرُوا): In al-Mukhtār: "qatara ʿalā ʿiyālihi: he was stingy toward them in spending; its pattern is ḍaraba and dakhala (yaqtiru, yaqturu), and qattara taqtīran and aqtara also: three forms." It has been read with a fatḥa on the first letter and with a ḍamma.
(قَواماً): with a fatḥa on the qāf and with a kasra; it has been read both ways. Qawām with a fatḥa is justice between two things because both extremes are straight; the counterpart of qawām from istiqāma is sawāʾ from istiwāʾ. Qiwām with a kasra is that by which a thing is upheld; one says "you are our qiwām" in the sense of that by which a need is met, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it.
(أَثاماً): al-athām is like al-wabāl and al-nakāl in pattern and meaning: the recompense of ithm, which is sin itself. He said:
جزى الله ابن عروة حيث أمسى ... عقوقا والعقوق له أثام
(Gloss: "May Allah recompense Ibn ʿUrwa, wherever he spent the evening, with disobedience; and disobedience has its recompense.")
In al-Mukhtār: "athamahu Allāh fī kadhā, with a short alif, yaʾthimuhu with a ḍamma on the thāʾ and with a kasra, athāman: He counted it against him as a sin, so he is maʾthūm. Al-Farrāʾ said: athamahu Allāh yaʾthimuhu ithman and athāman: He recompensed him with the recompense of sin, so he is maʾthūm, that is, recompensed with the recompense of his sin."

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ إِذا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكانَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ قَواماً): «والذين» is conjoined to what precedes; «إذا» is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause «أنفقوا» is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause «لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا» has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl-wāw; «كان» is a defective past verb and its noun is a latent pronoun, that is, "and the spending was"; «بين» is an adverbial attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of «قواما»; «ذلك» is its muḍāf ilayhi; and «قواما» is the khabar of «كان». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The two accusatives, I mean «بين ذلك قواما», may both be khabars together; or «بين ذلك» may be made superfluous and «قواما» the (real) predicate; or the adverbial may be the khabar and «قواما» an emphatic ḥāl."
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ): «والذين» is likewise conjoined to what precedes; the clause «لا يدعون» is the ṣila; «مع الله» is attached to «يدعون»; «إله» is a direct object and «آخر» an adjective.
(وَلا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلا يَزْنُونَ): «ولا يقتلون» is conjoined to «ولا يدعون»; «النفس» is a direct object; «التي» is an adjective; the clause «حرم الله» is the ṣila; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «بالحق» is attached to «يقتلون» or to an omitted element, a ḥāl, so the exception is from the most general of circumstances, that is, "except as those entitled"; «ولا يزنون» is conjoined.
(وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثاماً يُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهاناً): the wāw is a conjunction; «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; «يفعل» is the protasis and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to «من»; «ذلك» is a direct object; «يلق» is the apodosis and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; «أثاما» is a direct object; «يضاعف» is a badal of «يلق», because the two are of one meaning; the discussion of substituting a verb for a verb will come in the section on Benefits, because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting of the recompense. «له» is attached to «يضاعف»; «العذاب» is a nāʾib fāʿil; «يوم القيامة» is an adverbial also attached to «يضاعف»; «يخلد» is conjoined to «يضاعف»; «فيه» is attached to «يخلد»; and «مهانا» is a ḥāl from the agent of «يخلد».
(إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صالِحاً): «إلا» is a particle of exception; «من» is a connected exception (of the same kind), in the position of accusative; the clause «تاب» is the ṣila; «آمن» is conjoined to «تاب», and likewise «عمل»; «عملا» is an absolute object or a direct object, and «صالحا» is an adjective.
(فَأُوْلئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): the fāʾ is a linking fāʾ because of the scent of conditionality in the relative noun; «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, the demonstrative referring to the relative noun, which is «من», the plural being in view of its meaning; the clause «يبدل» is the khabar of «أولئك»; «الله» is the agent and «سيئاتهم» the object; «حسنات» is a second object of «يبدل», or accusative by removal of the preposition. In «وكان», the wāw is resumptive; «كان» and its noun; «غفورا» is its first khabar and «رحيما» its second khabar.
(وَمَنْ تابَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتاباً): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; «من» is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; «تاب» is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis; «عمل» is conjoined to «تاب»; «صالحا» is an adjective of an omitted absolute object or an omitted direct object, that is, "a righteous deed". «فإنه»: the fāʾ links the response, because it is a nominal clause; «إن» and its noun; the clause «يتوب» is the khabar; «إلى الله» is a preposition phrase attached to «يتوب»; and «متابا» is an absolute object, because it is a maṣdar mīmī (a verbal noun with a prefixed mīm).

* Benefits:
Substituting a verb for a verb:
A noun, a verb and a clause may each be a badal of its like, and the rules of the badal apply to it. It may be a total substitute (badal kull min kull) or a congruent substitute (badal muṭābiq), as in His saying, the Exalted, «ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما يضاعف»: «يضاعف» is a badal of «يلق», a total or congruent substitute. Al-Khalīl said: because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting of the recompense. A partial substitute (badal baʿḍ), for example: "If you pray, prostrate to Allah, He will have mercy on you": "tasjud" is a badal of "tuṣalli", a partial substitute for a whole. And a substitute by inclusion (badal ishtimāl), as in his saying:
إن عليّ الله أن تبايعا ... تؤخذ كرها أو تجيء طائعا
(Gloss: "By Allah, it is incumbent on me that you pledge allegiance: you will be taken by force, or you will come willingly.")
because being taken by force and coming willingly are among the attributes of pledging allegiance. «الله» is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "wa-Allāhi"; «أن تبايعا» is the noun of «إن», and the alif in «تبايعا» is the alif of prolongation (iṭlāq); it is from bāyaʿa, that is, to covenant; «علي» is attached to the khabar; and «تؤخذ» and what is conjoined to it is a substitute by inclusion in terms of meaning. As for substituting a clause, it is regular in the congruent substitute, for example "qaʿadtu jalastu fī dār Zayd" (I sat, I stayed, in Zayd's house).
And in the partial substitute for a whole, as in His saying, the Exalted: «أمدكم بما تعلمون: أمدكم بأنعام وبنين»: the second clause «أمدكم» is more specific than the first in terms of their objects, so it falls within the first, because «ما تعلمون» includes livestock and other things. And a substitute by inclusion, as in his saying:
أقول له ارحل لا تقيمنّ عندنا ... وإلا فكن في السر والجهر مسلما
(Gloss: "I say to him: depart, do not stay with us; otherwise be, in secret and in public, a man at peace.")
Here «لا تقيمن عندنا» is a badal of inclusion from «ارحل» because of the necessary relation between them; it is not emphasis (tawkīd), because their wordings differ, nor a partial substitute, because it is not included in the first, nor a total substitute, because it is not counted as such, as has preceded.
A clause may also substitute for a single word as a total substitute, as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إلى الله أشكو بالمدينة حاجة ... وبالشام أخرى كيف يلتقيان
(Gloss: "To Allah I complain of a need in Medina and another in Syria: how can the two meet?")
He substituted the clause «كيف يلتقيان» for «حاجة» and «أخرى», which are single words. As for substituting a single word for a clause, Abū Ḥayyān stated explicitly in al-Baḥr that a single word may substitute for a clause, as in His saying, the Exalted: «ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما»: «قيما» is a badal of the clause «لم يجعل له عوجا», because it is in the sense of a single word, that is, "He made it straight".

dervis-irab:35-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرَّسِّ): the name of a particular well. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is the lined well, and the plural is al-rasās, and from it is the saying of the poet:
وهم سائرون إلى أرضهم ... تنابلة يحفرون الرساسا
(They are travelling to their land, stunted men digging wells.)
It is also said: al-Rass is a village. The People of al-Rass were a people among the idol-worshippers, owners of wells and cattle, to whom Allah sent Shuʿayb, and he called them to Islam, but they persisted in their tyranny and in harming him. It is also said that they were the companions of the prophet Ḥanẓala ibn Ṣafwān, who were afflicted by the ʿanqāʾ, whose discussion will come: it lived on their mountain and swooped upon their children, snatching them whenever game was scarce for it; so Ḥanẓala invoked against it and the thunderbolt struck it. Then they killed Ḥanẓala and were destroyed. It is also said that they were the People of the Trench, and al-rass is the trench. It is also said that al-Rass is in Antioch, where they killed Ḥabīb the carpenter.
The ʿanqāʾ is the largest of birds, so named for the length of its neck. It is called ʿanqāʾ mughrib (in annexation) or al-ʿanqāʾ al-mughrib and al-mughriba (as an adjective). It is a bird of unknown body, never found, and a calamity; of the report of a thing's destruction and ruin one says: "the ʿanqāʾ mughrib has flown off with it". It was called mughrib either for bringing something strange, namely snatching children — and it is said that it snatched a bride — or for its ghurūb, i.e. its disappearance; mughrib is with ḍamma or fatḥa on the mīm; and other things are said whose enumeration would be long.
It is also said that al-Rass is water and date palms belonging to Banū Asad; and it is said to be snow piled up on the mountains; and al-Rass is the name of a valley. Zuhayr said:
بكرن بكورا واستحرنا بسحرة ... فهن ووادي الرس كاليد في الفم
(They set out early in the morning, and we set out at the last hour of night; and they and the valley of al-Rass are like the hand in the mouth.)
(تَبَّرْنا): We crushed, and from it comes al-tibr, for the fragments of gold and silver.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ وَجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أَخاهُ هارُونَ وَزِيراً) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to confirm the preceding consolation of Muḥammad ﷺ by relating what befell the prophets and what they suffered from their peoples.
The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, and قَدْ is a particle of confirmation; آتَيْنا is a verb, an agent, and مُوسَى a direct object; الْكِتابَ is the second object of آتَيْنا; وَجَعَلْنا is conjoined to آتَيْنا; مَعَهُ is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted element which is the second object of جَعَلْنا; أَخاهُ is the first object of جَعَلْنا; هارُونَ is a badal of أَخاهُ or an ʿaṭf bayān; and وَزِيراً is a ḥāl — or you may make وَزِيراً the second object and attach the adverbial to an omitted accusative ḥāl. (فَقُلْنَا اذْهَبا إِلَى الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا فَدَمَّرْناهُمْ تَدْمِيراً) فَقُلْنَا is conjoined to what precedes; قُلْنَا is a verb and an agent; the clause اذْهَبا is the quoted speech; إِلَى الْقَوْمِ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اذْهَبا; الَّذِينَ is an adjective of الْقَوْمِ; the clause كَذَّبُوا is a ṣila; بِآياتِنا is attached to كَذَّبُوا; the fāʾ is a conjunction on an omitted element, i.e. "so they went to them, and they denied them both, so We destroyed them"; دَمَّرْناهُمْ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; and تَدْمِيراً is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْناهُمْ) وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ is the direct object of an omitted verb that what follows explains, i.e. "and We drowned the people of Noah"; you may also conjoin it to the hāʾ in دَمَّرْناهُمْ, i.e. "and We destroyed the people of Noah". لَمَّا is an adverbial in the sense of "when" or a linking particle implying condition in every case, and an allusion to it has already been made; كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; and the clause أَغْرَقْناهُمْ is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and so has no position. (وَجَعَلْناهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ آيَةً وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلظَّالِمِينَ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) وَجَعَلْناهُمْ is conjoined to what precedes; لِلنَّاسِ is the second object of جَعَلْناهُمْ and آيَةً the first object of it; وَأَعْتَدْنا is conjoined to جَعَلْناهُمْ; لِلظَّالِمِينَ is attached to أَعْتَدْنا, and it admits of designation and specification, in which case it is a putting of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, to record against them the description of wrongdoing. (وَعاداً وَثَمُودَ وَأَصْحابَ الرَّسِّ وَقُرُوناً بَيْنَ ذلِكَ كَثِيراً) وَعاداً is the direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "We destroyed" or "We annihilated"; وَثَمُودَ and أَصْحابَ الرَّسِّ and قُرُوناً are conjoined to it; what is meant by قُرُوناً is peoples; and كَثِيراً is an adjective of قُرُوناً. (وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنا تَتْبِيراً) كُلًّا is a direct object of an omitted verb that meets ضَرَبْنا in meaning, i.e. "We warned and cautioned each", so it is accusative by occupation (ishtighāl), and the clause ضَرَبْنا is explicative, a past verb and an agent; لَهُ is attached to ضَرَبْنا; الْأَمْثالَ is a direct object; and كُلًّا is a direct object fronted before تَبَّرْنا, because it is free for it, not occupied with its pronoun; تَبَّرْنا is a verb and an agent, and تَتْبِيراً is a mafʿūl muṭlaq.
(وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ) The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قَدْ is a particle of confirmation; أَتَوْا is a verb and an agent; عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ is attached to أَتَوْا; الَّتِي is an adjective of الْقَرْيَةِ; the clause أُمْطِرَتْ is a ṣila; and مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of أُمْطِرَتْ, so it has the sense of "rains of evil". What is meant by "rain of evil" is stones. The meaning is that Quraysh passed many times by the dwellings of that village, which was destroyed by stones from the sky, during their journeys for trade. And in al-Qāmūs: «sāʾa sūʾan with fatḥa: he did to him what he dislikes, and al-sūʾ with ḍamma is a noun from it.» The village here is a generic noun, because it includes five villages in which the people of Lot lived, of which only one was saved; and it is said to be a single village called Sadhūm with the dotted dhāl or Sadūm with the undotted dāl; all of this has been covered before. (أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَها بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُوراً) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) that implies denial; taqrīr is leading the addressee to acknowledge what he knows. The fāʾ is a conjunction conjoining what follows it to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Were they not looking at it? Did they not see it several times during their stopping by it, so as to take a lesson from the fates of those before them and from the incalculable punishment that their persistence in error and riding the back of excess brought upon them?" The clause يَرَوْنَها is the khabar of يَكُونُوا; بَلْ is a particle of turning away; كانُوا and its noun; the clause لا يَرْجُونَ is its khabar; and نُشُوراً is a direct object.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «لا يرجون نشورا» is a figurative usage (majāz) for anticipation; and anticipating a thing can be in good and in evil. Since the reality of hope (rajāʾ) is awaiting good, with the joy in it and what is dear to the soul, there is need to direct the "hope" as we have said, and because hope for the resurrection is not conceivable of the disbelievers.
Some have run the speech on the literal sense and said that rajāʾ here means fear; this is sheer strain, and in the figurative reading there is ample room.
2- In His saying «فقلنا اذهبا» up to «فدمرناهم تدميرا» is ellipsis (al-ḥadhf). Do you not see how the answer to the command was omitted in this verse? Its implied form is: "so We said: Go to the people who denied Our signs; so they went to them, and they denied them both, so We destroyed them utterly."

dervis-irab:72-77.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِراماً): «والذين» is conjoined to the preceding relative nouns; the clause «لا يشهدون» is the ṣila. As for «الزور»: if «يشهدون» is in the sense of the well-known giving of testimony, then «الزور» is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "bi-l-zūr"; if «يشهدون» is in the sense of "attend", then «الزور» is a direct object. «وإذا»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause «مروا» is genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; «مروا» is a verb and agent; «باللغو» is attached to «مروا»; the second clause «مروا» has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and «كراما» is a ḥāl, that is, they raised themselves above standing at it and taking part in it.
(وَالَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِّرُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها صُمًّا وَعُمْياناً): the clause «لم يخروا» has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «عليها» is attached to «يخروا»; the meaning of this negation will come in the section on Rhetoric; «صما» is a ḥāl and «عميانا» a second ḥāl.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا هَبْ لَنا مِنْ أَزْواجِنا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِماماً): conjoined to what precedes. «ربنا» is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; «هب» is an imperative verb containing the meaning of supplication; «لنا» is attached to «هب»; «من أزواجنا» is a ḥāl, and the discussion of this tajrīd (abstraction) will come in the section on Rhetoric; «قرة أعين» is the object of «هب», and it has already been mentioned that qurrat al-ʿayn is its delight, what is meant being that by which delight is attained; the secret of using the small plural of "eyes" will come in the section on Rhetoric. «اجعلنا» is an imperative verb containing the meaning of supplication, its agent latent, and "us" the first object; «للمتقين» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «إماما»; and «إماما» is a second direct object. There are four views on it:
1- That it is a maṣdar like qiyām and ṣiyām, so it is not pluralised, and the implied form is "possessors of an imām".
2- That it is the plural of imāma, like qilāda and qilād.
3- That it is the plural of āmm, from amma yaummu.
4- That it is a singular used instead of aʾimma (imams), as He said, the Exalted: «نخرجكم طفلا».
(أُوْلئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ بِما صَبَرُوا وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وَسَلاماً): the clause is a ḥāl from «المتقين», or the khabar of «عباد الرحمن» according to one of the two views. «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يجزون الغرفة» is its khabar; «الغرفة» is a second direct object of «يجزون», and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, which is the first object. «بما» is attached to «يجزون»; «ما» is maṣdar and the bāʾ is causal, that is, because of their patience through the hardships of acts of obedience, their keeping away from desires and their enduring of struggles. «يلقون» is conjoined to «يجزون»; «فيها» is a ḥāl; «تحية» is a second direct object of «يلقون», because it is passive, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; «سلاما» is conjoined to «تحية».
(خالِدِينَ فِيها حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقاماً): «خالدين» is a ḥāl; «فيها» is attached to «خالدين»; «حسنت» is a past verb whose agent is latent, referring to «الغرفة»; «مستقرا» is a tamyīz; «مقاما» is conjoined to «مستقرا»; and the clause «حسنت» is a second ḥāl from «الغرفة».
(قُلْ ما يَعْبَؤُا بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلا دُعاؤُكُمْ): «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an absolute object; «يعبأ» is an imperfect verb; «بكم» is attached to «يعبأ»; «ربي» is the agent, that is, He cares about you, takes notice of you and raises your mention on account of your worship, and were it not for your worship you would be nothing to be heeded. It is permissible that «ما» be negative, and «لولا» a particle of prevention due to existence; «دعاؤكم» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted, and the response of «لولا» is omitted, as we have implied previously; «دعاؤكم» is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, and the object is omitted, that is, "Him".
(فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزاماً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is: since I have informed you that I do not count you and do not give you any weight except on account of your worship, you have opposed My ruling by your denial, so you will bear the responsibility of your denial. «يكون» is a defective imperfect verb and its noun is "it", that is, the denial; «لزاما» is its khabar, a maṣdar in the sense of an active participle, that is, "clinging to you".

* Rhetoric:
1- Negation and affirmation:
In His saying, the Exalted, «لم يخرّوا عليها صما وعميانا» there is negation and affirmation. He affirmed the falling down (khurūr), for they have long fallen down prostrating and humble in the stillness of the night and amid the darkness; but when they fall down prostrating their eyes and ears are sound, so they see only sights of awe, the wonders of divinity and the radiant lights of splendour, and hear only verses repeating in their ears and stirring in their imaginations, so that creation is signs and lessons, and sin has neither eye nor trace. You say "Zayd does not meet me walking," which negates the walking, not the meeting. The wording of Ibn Qutayba: "The meaning is: they did not turn a blind eye to them as if deaf, not hearing them, and blind, not seeing them."
2- Reprimand of the disbelievers:
In it also is a denunciation and reprimand of the disbelievers, because they are deaf, dumb and blind; they do not benefit from what they read, nor take lessons from what they witness, and what they hear does not pass beyond their ears.
3- Indefiniteness and reduction:
In His saying, the Exalted, «قرة أعين» there are two subtleties. The first is indefiniteness (tankīr); He leaned toward it only for the sake of the indefiniteness of «قرة», and the muḍāf can be made indefinite only by making the muḍāf ilayhi indefinite, so that the delight is neither finite nor limited. [Translator's note: the source says "two subtleties" but names only the first as such and then discusses the second, the reduction of the number of eyes, in what follows.] He reduced the eyes, that is, used the plural of paucity (jamʿ al-qilla), because the eyes of the God-fearing are few relative to others; this is indicated by His saying «وقليل من عبادي الشكور». There is another aspect, perhaps more eloquent than the foregoing, which is that what is quoted is the speech of each one of the God-fearing, as if He had said: "each one of the God-fearing says, 'make for us from our offspring a delight of eyes'"; for though the God-fearing are few relative to others, in themselves they are of a large number, and what is considered in using the plural of paucity is that the totality be few in itself, not by relation and comparison.

dervis-irab:41-44.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُواً) The wāw is resumptive; إِذا is a future adverbial implying condition; the clause رَأَوْكَ is genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; إِنْ is negative; يَتَّخِذُونَكَ is a verb, an agent and an object; the clause has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and the apodosis is not accompanied by the fāʾ because إِذا alone among the conditional particles has the property that its negated apodosis is not accompanied by the fāʾ, unlike the other particles. إِلَّا is a particle of restriction and هُزُواً is the second direct object of يَتَّخِذُونَكَ.
(أَهذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا) The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the wāw in يَتَّخِذُونَكَ, on the implication of "saying", i.e. "saying"; the hamza is for the interrogative of denial; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause بَعَثَ is a ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "sent him"; اللَّهُ is the agent of بَعَثَ; and رَسُولًا is a ḥāl — it may have the sense of "sent" (mursal), or be a maṣdar from which a muḍāf is omitted, i.e. "possessor of a message", and it is risāla. In the demonstrative is a sense of contempt, because it is for the near. (إِنْ كادَ لَيُضِلُّنا عَنْ آلِهَتِنا لَوْلا أَنْ صَبَرْنا عَلَيْها) إِنْ is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), and the clause is the remainder of what they said; its noun is omitted, i.e. "that he"; the clause كادَ is its khabar — it may also be left inoperative; the noun of كادَ is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the lām is the distinguishing lām between the negative إِنْ and the lightened إِنْ; the clause يُضِلُّنا is the khabar of كادَ, an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and نا a direct object; عَنْ آلِهَتِنا is attached to يُضِلُّنا; لَوْلا is a particle of prevention due to existence implying condition; أَنْ and what is within its scope is a mubtadaʾ; عَلَيْها is attached to صَبَرْنا; the khabar is omitted, i.e. "existent", and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "he would have turned us away from them". (وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذابَ مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive and the speech is resumptive, brought as a reply to them from Allah the Exalted; سَوْفَ is a particle of futurity; يَعْلَمُونَ is an imperfect verb and an agent; حِينَ is an adverbial of time attached to يَعْلَمُونَ; the clause يَرَوْنَ is in the position of the genitive by annexation of the adverbial to it; مَنْ is an interrogative and a mubtadaʾ; أَضَلُّ is its khabar; سَبِيلًا is a tamyīz; and the clause is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of يَعْلَمُونَ, which has been suspended from operating by the interrogative, i.e. "Are they, or the believers?" (أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ) The hamza is interrogative; رَأَيْتَ is a verb and an agent, meaning "tell me"; مَنِ is a relative noun, the first object of رَأَيْتَ; the clause اتَّخَذَ is a ṣila; إِلهَهُ is the second direct object of اتَّخَذَ and هَواهُ the first direct object; the second object was fronted because it is more important and out of concern for it, because it is the axis on which the astonishment turns; a subtle discussion of this fronting will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا) The clause is in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of رَأَيْتَ; the hamza is for the interrogative of denial, to make hopeless of their faith; the fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied element, i.e. "are you eager for his faith"; أَنْتَ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تَكُونُ its khabar; the noun of تَكُونُ is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; عَلَيْهِ is attached to وَكِيلًا; and وَكِيلًا is the khabar of تَكُونُ. (أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ) أَمْ is a conjunction equivalent to بَلْ with the hamza, so it is munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive), and the implied hamza is for denial; أنّ and what is within its scope fill the place of the two objects of تَحْسَبُ; the clause يَسْمَعُونَ is the khabar of أنّ; أَوْ is a conjunction; and يَعْقِلُونَ is conjoined to يَسْمَعُونَ. (إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا) إِنْ is negative; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; إِلَّا is a particle of restriction; the kāf is the khabar of هُمْ; بَلْ is a conjunction and a particle of turning away; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and أَضَلُّ its khabar; and سَبِيلًا is a tamyīz.

* Rhetoric:
1- Fronting (al-taqdīm):
In His saying «اتخذ إلهه هواه» is fronting, for the second object has been fronted, the original being "he took desire as a god", out of concern for it, as in your saying "I thought departing Zayd" when your concern is with the one departing. Beside this point there is a second, which is giving the sense of restriction. Before أرأيت entered, the speech was a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, the mubtadaʾ being هواه and the khabar إلهه, and fronting the khabar, as you know, gives restriction; it is as though He said: "Have you seen one who takes as his object of worship nothing but his desire?" — which is more eloquent in censuring and rebuking him. Some of the grammarians have claimed that there is no fronting or delaying in the speech and that they are simply the two objects of اتخاذ with no fronting or delaying, because they are equal in definiteness. But this is a mere illusion; for even if they are equal in definiteness, it escaped the holders of this claim that the second object is the one clothed in the newly occurring state, i.e. "Have you seen one who made his desire a god for himself, without regard to it, and built upon it the matter of his religion, turning altogether away from hearing the dazzling proof and the shining evidence?"
2-

Simile-parable (al-tamthīl):
In His saying «إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا» is the art of tamthīl. An allusion to this art has already been made; it comes down to this: the speaker intends a meaning and does not express it with its specific wording, nor with the two wordings of allusion (ishāra) and consequence (irdāf), but with a wording a little further than the wording of irdāf, which can serve as a parable for the specific wording, since a parable does not resemble the thing paralleled in every respect, and if two parallels were alike in every respect they would be one. Of tamthīl there is also another kind, taken up by those who came after Qudāma, which is that a thing is mentioned to serve as an example of the intended meaning even if its meaning and wording differ from the intended meaning and wording — as though they, in their steadfastness upon misguidance, were like cattle and beasts, indeed further astray in way, because beasts are led by whoever tends them and distinguish whoever does good to them from whoever does ill to them, whereas these have sunk to a depth lower than this.
Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ, in his book called Taḥrīr al-Taḥbīr, extracted the proverbs of Abū Tammām from his poetry and found them to be three hundred and ninety and a half verses [Translator's note: literally "ninety halves and three hundred verses"; the wording is translated as it stands], and he gathered the proverbs of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī and found them to be one hundred and a half verses and four hundred [Translator's note: literally "a hundred halves and four hundred verses"]. We have mentioned in earlier parts of this book a number of the proverbs of al-Mutanabbī, and here we mention another group of them:
لعل عتبك محمود عواقبه ... فربما صحت الأجسام بالعلل
(Perhaps your reproach will have praiseworthy consequences; for bodies are sometimes healed by ailments.)
and his saying:
ومكايد السفهاء واقعة بهم ... وعداوة الشعراء بئس المقتنى
(The schemes of fools fall upon themselves; and the enmity of poets is a wretched possession.)
and his saying:
لا يعجبن مضيما حسن بزته ... وهل تروق دفينا جودة الكفن
(Let the beauty of his garb not please one wronged; does the quality of a shroud delight one who is buried?)
and his saying:
وانا الذي اجتلب المنية طرفه ... فمن المطالب والقتيل القاتل
(I am the one whose own glance drew death to him; so who is the pursuer, when the slain is the slayer?)
and his saying:
وما كمد الحساد شيئا قصدته ... ولكنه من يرحم البحر يغرق
(The envious's grief is not something I aimed at; but whoever pities the sea drowns.)

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُباتاً): rest for the bodies through the cutting off of work. It is from al-sabt, i.e. cutting, so named for the cutting off of occupations in it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «al-subāt on the pattern of ghurāb is heavy sleep, and its origin is rest; from it one says sabata yasbutu, of the pattern qatala.» In al-Qāmūs it is of both patterns, qatala and ḍaraba, then it says: «al-subāt is sleep, or light sleep, or its beginning in the head until it reaches the heart.» al-Zamakhsharī said: «al-Subāt is death, and al-masbūt is the dead, because he is cut off from life; this is like His saying «وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل». If you say: why did you not explain it as rest? I say: the nushūr [rising] opposed to it refuses it with the refusal of the thirsty camel to a muddied watering place.» al-ʿAyūf among camels, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, is the one that smells the water and leaves it though thirsty; and in it also: «I made it turbid (ranniqtuhu tarnīqan), I clouded it.» In al-Lisān and al-Asās: «Allah made sleep subāt: death, and so-and-so became masbūt: dead.» In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: «al-Subāt: sleep, or its beginning; time; the man who is a calamity; and "the two sons of Subāt" are night and day, taken from the sense of time; sabata yasbutu of the two patterns qatala and ḍaraba, sabtan: he entered the Sabbath and attended to the matter of the Sabbath: he rested; sabata the thing: he cut it; sabata the head: he shaved it; and al-sabt is a maṣdar, and a day of the days of the week between Friday and Sunday, its plural being asbut and subūt; and al-sabt also means: the sleepers, the excellent horse, and the man who is a calamity.»
(الرِّياحَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The winds are four: the north (al-shamāl), which comes from the direction of Syria; the south (al-janūb), opposite it, which is the Yemeni wind; the third is the east wind (al-ṣabā), which comes from the rising place of the sun and is also called al-qabūl; and the fourth is the west wind (al-dabūr), which comes from the direction of the west. The word rīḥ is feminine for the most part, so one says hiya al-rīḥ; it may be masculine in the sense of air, so one says huwa al-rīḥ and habba al-rīḥ, reported by Abū Zayd.» Ibn al-Anbārī said: al-rīḥ is feminine with no sign in it, and so are all its names except al-iʿṣār (whirlwind), which is masculine.
(طَهُوراً): al-ṭahūr has two aspects in Arabic: an attribute and a noun that is not an attribute. The attribute is your saying māʾ ṭahūr like your saying ṭāhir; the noun is your saying, of that with which one purifies oneself, ṭahūr, like al-wuḍūʾ and al-wuqūd, for that with which one performs ablution and with which fire is kindled, as in your saying "a good wuḍūʾ", mentioned by Sībawayh.
(أَناسِيَّ): al-anāsī is the plural of insī or insān, like ẓarābī for ẓarbān, with the nūn changed to yāʾ; the original is anāsīn and ẓarābīn, and perhaps the second is preferable. Sībawayh said: «The yāʾ in insī is the yāʾ of attribution (nisba), and what contains it is not pluralised on faʿālī.» Ibn Mālik said: «Make faʿālī the plural for what is not of attribution.» Ibn Hishām and Ibn Mālik were firm that it is the plural of insān, not of insī. They said: qabāṭī as the plural of qibṭī and bakhātī as the plural of bukhtī are irregular. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-qibṭ are the people of Egypt, a man is qibṭī, and al-qibṭiyya are white thin garments of linen; and al-bukht among camels is Arabised, and it is also said to be Arabic, and a verse of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt is recited:
يهب الخيل والألوف ويسقي ... لبن البخت في قصاع الخلنج
(He gives away horses and thousands, and serves the milk of the bukht camels in bowls of khalanj wood.)

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شاءَ لَجَعَلَهُ ساكِناً) A resumptive speech, brought to begin citing perceptible proofs of His oneness. Five proofs will come: the first is the lengthening of the shade; the second, the making of night a garment; the third, the sending of the winds; the fourth, the letting loose of the two seas; and the fifth, the creation of mankind from water. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); لَمْ is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تَرَ, i.e. "look", is an imperfect verb jussive by لَمْ, and here it is of sight; إِلى رَبِّكَ is attached to تَرَ with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "at the handiwork of your Lord", because the intention is not seeing the essence of Allah; كَيْفَ is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "Have you not looked at the handiwork of your Lord, how He extended the shade", that is, in what state; and the meaning of "extended the shade" is that He made it extend and spread out, so that people benefit from it. al-Zajjāj preferred that the seeing be of the heart and the meaning be "Have you not known"; he said: this is preferable because if we make the shade among the things seen, the effect of Allah's power in extending it is, by agreement, not seen, but is known in that every visible thing has an effector; so taking the word as seeing of the heart is preferable. كَيْفَ has been suspended from the operation of تَرَ, so the clause مَدَّ الظِّلَّ is in the position of the accusative as the second object, and on the first view it is resumptive.
وَلَوْ: the wāw is circumstantial; لَوْ is conditional; شاءَ is a past verb with a latent agent; the lām falls in the answer to لَوْ; the clause جَعَلَهُ has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the hāʾ is the first object of جَعَلَ; and ساكِناً is its second object, i.e. fixed, by making the sun in a single position, or constant and not vanishing. (ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا الشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًا) ثُمَّ here is for the gradation between the times of appearance and is not for temporal delay, because that is not valid here; it is taken as figurative, as will come in the chapter on rhetoric. جَعَلْنا is a verb and an agent; الشَّمْسَ is a direct object; عَلَيْهِ is a ḥāl; and دَلِيلًا is the second direct object, i.e. were it not for the sun, the shade would not be known. (ثُمَّ قَبَضْناهُ إِلَيْنا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً) And ثُمَّ here is likewise for gradation among the three matters, namely the extending of the shade, its stillness and its drawing in, as though the second were greater than the first and the third greater than both. قَبَضْناهُ is a verb, an agent and a direct object; إِلَيْنا is attached to قَبَضْناهُ; قَبْضاً is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and يَسِيراً an adjective. The meaning of His drawing it in gently is: according to the rising of the sun, so that thereby the interests of the cosmos are ordered. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباساً وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً وَجَعَلَ النَّهارَ نُشُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause جَعَلَ is a ṣila; لَكُمُ is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of لِباساً; اللَّيْلَ is the first object of جَعَلَ and لِباساً its second object; وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً is conjoined to what precedes; and وَجَعَلَ النَّهارَ نُشُوراً is likewise conjoined, i.e. a dispersal in which people spread out to earn their livelihood. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ) بُشْراً is a ḥāl; بَيْنَ is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of بُشْراً; and يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ is a muḍāf ilayhi; the verification of this will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً طَهُوراً) Conjoined to what precedes, and in it is an intimation that purifying the outward entails purifying the inward, and in that is the utmost of favour and blessing. (لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنا أَنْعاماً وَأَناسِيَّ كَثِيراً) The lām of cause is attached to أَنْزَلْنا to explain the reason for sending it down; بِهِ is attached to نُحْيِيَ; بَلْدَةً is a direct object; مَيْتاً is an adjective of بَلْدَةً, in which masculine and feminine are alike, or because it is masculine in the sense of "town" (balad), as in «فسقناه إلى بلد ميت»; وَنُسْقِيَهُ is conjoined to نُحْيِيَ, following it in the accusative; one says saqāhu and asqāhu, and both take two objects; مِمَّا is attached to an omitted ḥāl; أَنْعاماً is the second direct object of نُسْقِيَهُ; and أَناسِيَّ كَثِيراً is conjoined to أَنْعاماً. The secret of placing the cattle before the humans will come in the chapter on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Fronting and delaying (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr):
In His saying «وأنزلنا من السماء ماء» up to His saying «وأناسي كثيرا» is the art of fronting and delaying, a wondrous art, subtle in approach and hidden in its indication. It is of two kinds: one that concerns the indication of words to meanings, and one that concerns the degree of precedence in mention, and the verse we are dealing with belongs to it. He put the life of the earth and the watering of the cattle before the watering of humans, though they are higher in rank, because the life of the earth is the cause of the life of the cattle and of humans; since it is of such a degree, it was placed first in mention. And since cattle are among the means of livelihood and life for people, He put them first in mention before people, because the life of people is through the life of their land and their cattle; so He put first the watering of what is the cause of their growth and livelihood, before their own watering.
2- In His saying «ثم جعلنا» and «ثم قبضناه» is an explicit, derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya), in which the word of the thing likened to — distance and delay — is borrowed for the thing likened, namely the gradation of the matters.
2- And in His saying «بين يدي رحمته» is also a metaphor, i.e. before the rain; more on this will come.
